children.title: Sketch Orientation
children.top_down_role: Distinguishes sketches of variables, observations, and constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Space Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-oriented sketches that restrict optimization to an affine subspace of the decision space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\) with \(s\le n\). A variable-space sketch replaces the original problem by
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^s} f(x_0+Sp).
\]
Its trial points lie in \(x_0+\operatorname{range}(S)\). If the original model contains a matrix acting on variables, such as \(Ax\), the reduced model contains \(A(x_0+Sp)=Ax_0+(AS)p\); hence the sketch acts on the variable side by right multiplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-space sketch parameterizes trial points as x₀+Sp, reducing an n-dimensional problem to optimization over s subspace coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^s}f(x_0+Sp)\) searches only \(x_0+\operatorname{range}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Variable-space sketch or subspace basis matrix.
Base point of the affine trial space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-subspace formulation is mathematically precise and fits the definition container, but no inspectable source supports the sketch-orientation terminology or convention.

children.title: Data-Matrix Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches applied directly to input matrices or data collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Matrix Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row sketches of linear least-squares data and its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a linear least-squares problem with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a sketch \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\), where \(1\le s<m\), a data-matrix sketch forms \(\widetilde A=SA\) and \(\widetilde b=Sb\), then solves
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\frac12\lVert \widetilde A x-\widetilde b\rVert_2^2
=
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\frac12\lVert S(Ax-b)\rVert_2^2.
\]
Thus the observation dimension is reduced from \(m\) to \(s\), while the decision variable remains in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A data-matrix sketch left-multiplies both A and b by the same map, producing a least-squares problem with fewer rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert (SA)x-Sb\rVert_2=\lVert S(Ax-b)\rVert_2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Sketched data matrix and right-hand side.

children.title: Residual-Vector Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches applied to residual vectors arising from optimization models.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Vector Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sketches applied directly to the residual map of an optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be a residual map on a feasible domain \(X\), and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\), where \(1\le s<m\). The residual-vector sketch is the composed map \(r_S=S\circ r\), namely \(r_S(x)=Sr(x)\). For a loss \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^s\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), the associated sketched problem is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\phi(Sr(x)).
\]
In the Euclidean least-squares case, \(\phi(z)=\tfrac12\lVert z\rVert_2^2\), so the sketched objective is \(\tfrac12\lVert Sr(x)\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual-vector sketch composes the model residual with a lower-dimensional linear map before evaluating the loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_S(x)=Sr(x)\) is an \(s\)-dimensional residual used in \(\min_{x\in X}\phi(r_S(x))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct composition of a residual with a linear sketch

children.title: Data-to-Residual Transfer
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which data-level sketch quality supports residual-level fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-to-Residual Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic correspondence between row-sketched affine data and sketched residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x)=Ax-b\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\). Define \(\widetilde A=SA\), \(\widetilde b=Sb\), and \(\widetilde r(x)=\widetilde A x-\widetilde b\). Linearity gives
\[
\widetilde r(x)=(SA)x-Sb=S(Ax-b)=Sr(x)
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Consequently, sketching the data pair \((A,b)\) and then forming its affine residual is exactly equivalent to first forming the residual and then applying the same row sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine residuals, sketching A and b is exactly the same operation as sketching Ax−b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((SA)x-Sb=S(Ax-b)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer identity is correct, explicit, and appropriately classified as a property, but the record has no inspectable source for its placement in the sketch taxonomy.

children.title: Constraint-System Sketches
children.top_down_role: Reduced representations formed from optimization constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-System Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation sketches for systems of linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the inequality system \(Ax\le b\), with inequalities interpreted componentwise, where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Given \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\) with nonnegative entries, its constraint-system sketch is
\[
SAx\le Sb.
\]
Each sketched row is a nonnegative linear combination of original inequalities. Therefore every point feasible for \(Ax\le b\) is feasible for \(SAx\le Sb\). The sketched system generally defines an outer relaxation; negative entries in \(S\) do not preserve this implication in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative row sketch aggregates linear inequalities, yielding an outer relaxation that contains every originally feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax\le b\Longrightarrow SAx\le Sb\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative combinations preserve valid inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonnegative aggregation correctly preserves componentwise inequalities and yields an outer relaxation, but the proposed constraint-sketch definition lacks an authoritative citation.

children.title: Equation-System Sketches
children.top_down_role: Reduced representations formed from linear or nonlinear equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Equation-System Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row sketches that aggregate equations in a linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a linear equation system \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\), the equation-system sketch is
\[
SAx=Sb,
\]
equivalently \(S(Ax-b)=0\). Every solution of the original system solves the sketched system. Conversely, a sketched solution need only have residual \(Ax-b\) in \(\ker S\), so the sketched solution set can be strictly larger unless the sketch is injective on all attainable residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equation-system sketch takes linear combinations of equations; original solutions remain feasible, but spurious sketched solutions may appear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\Longrightarrow SAx=Sb\), while \(SAx=Sb\Longleftrightarrow Ax-b\in\ker S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equation aggregation and kernel characterization are correct and fit the definition container, but no inspectable source supports the terminology.

children.title: Feasibility Transfer Across Sketches
children.top_down_role: How reduced-system feasibility relates to feasibility in the original system.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Transfer Across Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for transferring feasibility back from a sketched consistent equation system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(Ax=b\) is consistent and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\). The original and sketched equation systems have identical feasible sets precisely when
\[
\ker S\cap\operatorname{range}(A)=\{0\}.
\]
Indeed, consistency supplies \(x_\star\) with \(Ax_\star=b\), so every attainable residual has the form \(A(x-x_\star)\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). Hence \(S(Ax-b)=0\) forces \(Ax-b=0\) exactly under the displayed injectivity condition. Without consistency, the corresponding exact condition must instead be imposed on the affine residual set \(\{Ax-b:x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent equation system, sketched and original feasibility coincide exactly when the sketch is injective on the range of A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:SAx=Sb\}=\{x:Ax=b\}\Longleftrightarrow\ker S\cap\operatorname{range}(A)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Column space of the equation matrix.
Residual directions erased by the sketch.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: injectivity on attainable residual directions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under consistency, the injectivity condition on range(A) is the correct necessary-and-sufficient condition. An authoritative source is still required for this nontrivial equivalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential linear embedding preserving all squared pairwise distances of an arbitrary finite Euclidean point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\in\mathbb{R}^N\) and \(\eta>0\). There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, if \(m>C\eta^{-2}\ln M\), then there exists \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}\) for which
\[
(1-\eta)\lVert x_j-x_\ell\rVert_2^2\leq \lVert B(x_j-x_\ell)\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\eta)\lVert x_j-x_\ell\rVert_2^2
\]
for all \(j,\ell\in[M]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any M points in Euclidean space, if the target dimension exceeds a universal constant times η⁻² log M, some linear map preserves every squared pairwise distance within factors 1−η and 1+η.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}\;\forall j,\ell\in[M]:\ (1-\eta)\lVert x_j-x_\ell\rVert_2^2\leq\lVert B(x_j-x_\ell)\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\eta)\lVert x_j-x_\ell\rVert_2^2

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Vector Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Johnson–Lindenstrauss norm preservation for one vector fixed independently of the random sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distribution over matrices \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\) has fixed-vector \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-preservation if, for every deterministic \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) chosen independently of \(S\),
\[
\Pr_S\!\left[(1-\varepsilon)\lVert v\rVert_2^2\le\lVert Sv\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert v\rVert_2^2\right]\ge1-\delta.
\]
The probability guarantee is pointwise in \(v\): it does not assert that one draw of \(S\) preserves all vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), nor does it cover a vector selected after observing that draw.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random sketch preserves the squared norm of any independently fixed vector within relative error ε, with failure probability at most δ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr_S[(1-\varepsilon)\lVert v\rVert_2^2\le\lVert Sv\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert v\rVert_2^2]\ge1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise fixed-vector guarantee is precise and distinguishes independent from adaptive vectors, but the squared-norm Johnson–Lindenstrauss convention has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous Johnson–Lindenstrauss preservation of all pairwise distances in a fixed finite set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a deterministic set with \(|V|=N\ge2\), chosen independently of a random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\). Finite-set \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-preservation means
\[
\Pr_S\!\left[\forall u,v\in V:\ (1-\varepsilon)\lVert u-v\rVert_2^2\le\lVert S(u-v)\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u-v\rVert_2^2\right]\ge1-\delta.
\]
If fixed-vector preservation fails with probability at most \(\eta\) for each unordered pair of distinct points, the union bound gives finite-set failure probability at most \(\binom{N}{2}\eta\). Therefore \(\eta\le\delta/\binom{N}{2}\) suffices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One random sketch simultaneously preserves every pairwise distance in a fixed set of at least two points; a union bound reduces this to fixed-vector guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(V\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is deterministic, independent of \(S\), and has \(|V|=N\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All \(\binom{N}{2}\) squared pairwise distances are preserved within factors \(1\pm\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Fixed finite set of embedded points.
Cardinality of the finite set, with N at least two.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-set Johnson–Lindenstrauss guarantee via union bound

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Subspace Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oblivious subspace embedding for one bounded-dimensional subspace fixed independently of the sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an integer \(d\) with \(1\le d\le n\). Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a deterministic linear subspace with \(\dim U\le d\), chosen independently of a random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\). The matrix \(S\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-embedding for \(U\) when
\[
(1-\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2\le\lVert Su\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2
\quad\text{for every }u\in U.
\]
A distribution over \(S\) is a fixed-subspace \((d,\varepsilon,\delta)\) oblivious subspace embedding if, for every fixed subspace \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\dim U\le d\), this event has probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-subspace oblivious embedding preserves every vector in any one subspace of dimension at most d that is fixed before the sketch is drawn.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le d\le n\) and \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a fixed linear subspace with \(\dim U\le d\), independent of \(S\).
\(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\) is sampled from the stated sketch distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr_S[\forall u\in U:(1-\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2\le\lVert Su\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2]\ge1-\delta\) for every fixed \(U\) with \(\dim U\le d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bounded-dimensional oblivious subspace embedding definition

knowledge_statements.title: Union-of-Subspaces Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous norm or distance preservation over a fixed finite union of subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=\{U_1,\ldots,U_L\}\) be fixed independently of \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\). Norm preservation on the union requires
\[
(1-\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2\le\lVert Su\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2
\quad\text{for every }u\in\bigcup_{i=1}^L U_i.
\]
To preserve distances between arbitrary \(u\in U_i\) and \(v\in U_j\), it suffices that \(S\) be an \(\varepsilon\)-embedding for every sum subspace \(U_i+U_j\), because \(u-v\in U_i+U_j\). Simultaneous probabilistic guarantees may be obtained by assigning failure probability across the finitely many required subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving a union requires simultaneous embeddings of its component subspaces; preserving cross-subspace distances is ensured by embedding every pairwise sum subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(U_1,\ldots,U_L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) are fixed linear subspaces independent of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Embedding every \(U_i+U_j\) implies \((1-\varepsilon)\lVert u-v\rVert_2^2\le\lVert S(u-v)\rVert_2^2\le(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u-v\rVert_2^2\) for all \(u\in U_i\), \(v\in U_j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance differences lie in pairwise sum subspaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise-sum condition correctly ensures cross-subspace distance preservation and fits the property container, but no union-of-subspaces embedding source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptively Generated Subspace Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why fixed-subspace embedding guarantees do not automatically cover sketch-dependent subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fixed-subspace preservation does not extend without qualification to a subspace selected after observing the sketch. Indeed, if \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\) with \(s<n\), then \(\ker S\ne\{0\}\). An adaptive rule can choose a nonzero \(u(S)\in\ker S\) and set \(U(S)=\operatorname{span}\{u(S)\}\). Then
\[
\lVert Su(S)\rVert_2^2=0<(1-\varepsilon)\lVert u(S)\rVert_2^2
\]
for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\). Thus a pointwise guarantee for every independently fixed subspace cannot be invoked for \(U(S)\); adaptive preservation requires fresh independent randomness, conditional guarantees, or a uniform guarantee over all possible outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch-dependent subspace can select a kernel direction and defeat norm preservation; fixed-subspace guarantees therefore require independence or stronger uniform control.
assumptions_latex: The adaptive rule may inspect \(S\) before choosing its subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a sketch-dependent one-dimensional \(U(S)\) on which the lower embedding inequality fails deterministically.

notation.meaning: Subspace chosen adaptively from the realized sketch.
Null space exposed by the sketch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-nullity counterexample is mathematically correct and the failure-boundary kind precisely fits the terminal container. A source is needed for the broader adaptive-sketching interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Residual Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform norm preservation on the affine residual set of a linear model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). The sketch \(S\) preserves the affine residuals of \((A,b)\) with distortion \(\varepsilon\) when
\[
(1-\varepsilon)\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2\leq \lVert S(Ax-b)\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Equivalently, \(S\) is a \((1\pm\varepsilon)\) squared-norm embedding of the affine set \(\{Ax-b:x\in\mathbb{R}^d\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch preserves affine residuals when it uniformly approximates every squared residual norm of the linear model within relative error ε.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert S(Ax-b)\rVert_2^2=(1\pm\varepsilon)\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2\) uniformly over \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports affine-residual embeddings.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically precise and fits the affine-residual leaf, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports it.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Matrix-Product Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frobenius-norm approximate multiplication for two fixed matrices sharing the sketched dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\), and \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). The sketch has \(\varepsilon\)-approximate matrix-product preservation for \((A,B)\) if
\[
\bigl\lVert A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SB-A^{\mathsf T}B\bigr\rVert_F
\leq \varepsilon\lVert A\rVert_F\lVert B\rVert_F.
\]
Thus all cross inner products are approximated collectively, because the \((i,j)\)-entry of the error is \(\langle Sa_i,Sb_j\rangle-\langle a_i,b_j\rangle\), where \(a_i\) and \(b_j\) are columns of \(A\) and \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate matrix multiplication requires the sketched cross-Gram matrix to approximate the original product in Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SB-A^{\mathsf T}B\rVert_F\leq\varepsilon\lVert A\rVert_F\lVert B\rVert_F\).

notation.meaning: Columns of the two input matrices.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports approximate matrix-product preservation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-matrix Frobenius-norm formulation is coherent and fits the leaf, but it has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Gram-Matrix Preservation
children.top_down_role: Fidelity of sketched Gram geometry over relevant vectors or subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Matrix Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm preservation of the Gram matrix generated by a fixed design matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\), \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), suppose \(S\) is a squared-norm embedding on \(\operatorname{range}(A)\):
\[
(1-\varepsilon)\lVert Ax\rVert_2^2\leq\lVert SAx\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\lVert Ax\rVert_2^2
\]
for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Then
\[
-\varepsilon A^{\mathsf T}A\preceq A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SA-A^{\mathsf T}A\preceq\varepsilon A^{\mathsf T}A.
\]
If \(A\) has full column rank, this is equivalent to \(\lVert (A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1/2}A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SA(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1/2}-I\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace embedding preserves the design Gram matrix in relative Loewner order, and in normalized operator norm when the design has full column rank.
assumptions_latex: Full column rank of \(A\) is required only for the normalized formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1-\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A\preceq A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SA\preceq(1+\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A\).

notation.meaning: Column space of the design matrix.
Euclidean or spectral norm, according to the argument.

review_flags: The statement is standard, but the supplied locators do not address sketch-based Gram preservation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Loewner-order and full-rank normalized formulations are standard and consistent, but no cited source supports the stated equivalence.

children.title: Local-Curvature Preservation
children.top_down_role: Fidelity of curvature information within local optimization models.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Curvature Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of Hessian quadratic forms when curvature factors through an embedded data subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\phi(Ax)\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\), \(\phi\) is twice differentiable, and \(W(x)=\nabla^2\phi(Ax)\succeq0\). Define \(H(x)=A^{\mathsf T}W(x)A\) and \(\widetilde H(x)=A^{\mathsf T}W(x)^{1/2}S^{\mathsf T}SW(x)^{1/2}A\). If \(S\) preserves squared norms on \(\operatorname{range}(W(x)^{1/2}A)\) with distortion \(\varepsilon\), then
\[
(1-\varepsilon)H(x)\preceq\widetilde H(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)H(x).
\]
The claim is local because both \(W(x)\) and its relevant embedded subspace may vary with \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embedding the weighted design subspace preserves the local Hessian in relative Loewner order.
assumptions_latex: \(f=\phi\circ A\) and \(\phi\) is twice differentiable at \(Ax\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1-\varepsilon)H(x)\preceq\widetilde H(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)H(x)\).

notation.meaning: Outer-function Hessian at the transformed point.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this weighted-subspace curvature-transfer formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-subspace argument fits local-curvature preservation, but the dimensions of S and the domain of ε are not introduced, and no source supports this formulation.

children.title: Curvature-Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where Gram fidelity does not provide adequate local-model fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Transfer Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature cannot transfer along directions that the sketch annihilates or fails to embed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=I_d\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert_2^2\), and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\) have \(m<d\). Then \(\nabla^2f(x)=I_d\), whereas the sketched quadratic \(\widetilde f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2\) has Hessian \(S^{\mathsf T}S\). Since \(\ker(S)\neq\{0\}\), choose \(v\neq0\) with \(Sv=0\). Consequently,
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)v=\lVert v\rVert_2^2>0,
\qquad
v^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\widetilde f(x)v=0.
\]
Thus no positive relative lower curvature bound can hold on the full space unless the relevant curvature-bearing subspace is embedded injectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a sketch annihilates a curved direction, the sketched model has zero curvature there, so full-space relative curvature preservation fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(c>0\) satisfies \(cI_d\preceq S^{\mathsf T}S\); hence positive relative lower curvature cannot transfer globally.
review_flags: Concrete countermechanism is self-contained, but no supporting source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and failure_boundary is the appropriate kind, but the record supplies no supporting source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized dense sketch with independent standard Gaussian entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A normalized Gaussian sketch from \(\mathbb{R}^n\) to \(\mathbb{R}^m\) is a random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) whose entries are independent and satisfy
\[
S_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,1/m).
\]
Equivalently, \(S=m^{-1/2}G\) with independent \(G_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\). For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), rotational invariance gives
\[
\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2\mathrel{\overset{d}{=}}\frac{\lVert x\rVert_2^2}{m}\chi_m^2,
\qquad
\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian sketch is a dense matrix of independent centered Gaussian entries scaled so every fixed vector preserves squared norm in expectation.
assumptions_latex: All matrix entries are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,1/m)\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) for fixed \(x\).

notation.meaning: Chi-squared distribution with m degrees of freedom.

review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover Gaussian sketch definitions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized Gaussian definition and fixed-vector chi-squared identity are consistent, but neither has a cited source or locator.

children.title: Subgaussian Sketches
children.top_down_role: Dense sketches drawn from subgaussian distribution families.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgaussian Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized dense sketch with independent isotropic subgaussian rows or entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dense normalized subgaussian sketch is a random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) of the form \(S=m^{-1/2}Z\), where the entries \(Z_{ij}\) are independent, have mean zero and variance one, and satisfy \(\lVert Z_{ij}\rVert_{\psi_2}\leq K\) for a finite constant \(K\). Here
\[
\lVert X\rVert_{\psi_2}=\inf\{t>0:\mathbb E\exp(X^2/t^2)\leq2\}.
\]
The normalization implies \(\mathbb E[S^{\mathsf T}S]=I_n\), so \(\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) for every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized subgaussian sketch has independent centered, unit-variance, uniformly subgaussian entries and preserves every fixed squared norm in expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[S^{\mathsf T}S]=I_n\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover subgaussian sketch definitions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entrywise normalized subgaussian definition is coherent and fits the leaf, but it lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bernoulli, Gaussian, and subgaussian random matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise distribution classes for dense random matrices and sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\) be random. It is Bernoulli if its entries are independent Rademacher variables, Gaussian if its entries are independent standard Gaussian variables, and subgaussian if its entries are independent, mean-zero, variance-one random variables for which common constants \(\beta,\kappa>0\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(|A_{jk}|\ge t)\le \beta e^{-\kappa t^2}\) for every \(t>0\), \(j\in[m]\), and \(k\in[N]\). Equivalently, with possibly different constants, the subgaussian condition can be expressed as \(\mathbb E e^{\theta A_{jk}}\le e^{c\theta^2}\) for all \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), with \(c\) uniform in \(j,k,N\). Gaussian and Bernoulli matrices are subgaussian, and subgaussian entries need not be identically distributed. Under the variance-one normalization, the smallest possible MGF constant is \(c=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bernoulli matrix has independent random-sign entries, a Gaussian matrix has independent standard-normal entries, and a subgaussian matrix has independent centered unit-variance entries satisfying a common Gaussian tail bound. The tail condition is equivalent, up to constants, to a uniform quadratic moment-generating-function bound. The entries need not be identically distributed, and unit variance forces the MGF constant to be at least one half.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\text{ is a random matrix}
\{A_{jk}\}_{j,k}\text{ are independent in each defined matrix class}
\mathbb E A_{jk}=0,\quad \mathbb E A_{jk}^{2}=1\quad\text{in the subgaussian case}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists\beta,\kappa>0:\ \mathbb P(|A_{jk}|\ge t)\le\beta e^{-\kappa t^2}\bigr)\Longleftrightarrow\bigl(\exists c>0:\ \mathbb E e^{\theta A_{jk}}\le e^{c\theta^2}\bigr),\quad c\ge\tfrac12\text{ under unit variance}.

children.title: Random-Sign Sketches
children.top_down_role: Dense sketches whose entries use randomized sign patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Sign Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rademacher specialization of a dense normalized subgaussian sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A normalized random-sign sketch is a matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) with independent entries
\[
S_{ij}=\frac{\xi_{ij}}{\sqrt m},
\qquad
\mathbb P(\xi_{ij}=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_{ij}=-1)=\tfrac12.
\]
Each entry has mean zero and variance \(1/m\), and therefore \(\mathbb E[S^{\mathsf T}S]=I_n\). In particular, for every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2.
\]
The variables \(\xi_{ij}\) are Rademacher variables and constitute a bounded subgaussian family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random-sign sketch uses independent ±1 entries scaled by the inverse square root of the number of rows.
assumptions_latex: The signs \(\xi_{ij}\) are mutually independent Rademacher variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{ij}=\xi_{ij}/\sqrt m\) and \(\mathbb E[S^{\mathsf T}S]=I_n\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover random-sign sketches.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Rademacher specialization is precise and definition is the correct kind, but no supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Tail-Behavior Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Distributional regimes affecting concentration quality, storage, and arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Behavior Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding dimension is governed by concentration strength, failure probability, and subspace complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=m^{-1/2}Z\) have independent, centered, isotropic subgaussian rows with subgaussian parameter at most \(K\), and let \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\) have orthonormal columns. There are universal constants \(C,c>0\) such that, for \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(0<\delta<1\),
\[
m\geq C K^4\varepsilon^{-2}\bigl(d+\log(1/\delta)\bigr)
\]
implies
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\lVert U^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SU-I_d\rVert_2>\varepsilon\right)\leq\delta.
\]
Hence weaker tail control, represented by larger \(K\), increases the sufficient sketch dimension, while bounded-sign and Gaussian families have constant-order \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stronger concentration permits smaller embedding dimension; larger subgaussian parameters increase the rows sufficient for a fixed distortion and failure probability.
assumptions_latex: The rows of \(Z\) are independent, centered, isotropic, and uniformly subgaussian with parameter \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\geq CK^4\varepsilon^{-2}(d+\log(1/\delta))\) suffices for an \(\varepsilon\)-embedding with failure probability at most \(\delta\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the embedded subspace.

review_flags: The dependence on the subgaussian parameter varies by convention and requires a matching authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sufficient row bound is a complexity bound rather than merely a principle, and its K-dependence depends on the precise subgaussian convention. A matching authoritative source is required before correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsampled Hadamard Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized sign preconditioning followed by a normalized Hadamard transform and uniform row sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(n\) admits an orthogonal normalized Hadamard matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfying \(H^{\mathsf T}H=I_n\). Let \(D\) be diagonal with independent Rademacher entries, and let \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) select \(m\) coordinates uniformly without replacement. A subsampled randomized Hadamard sketch is
\[
S=\sqrt{\frac{n}{m}}RHD.
\]
For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the scaling and uniform sampling give \(\mathbb E_R\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\), conditional on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SRHT randomly flips signs, applies an orthogonal Hadamard transform, uniformly samples output coordinates, and rescales to preserve norm in expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(H^{\mathsf T}H=I_n\) is a normalized Hadamard transform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\sqrt{n/m}RHD\) and \(\mathbb E_R\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover subsampled Hadamard sketches.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SRHT construction and conditional expectation identity are coherent, but no cited source with a specific locator supports them.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsampled Fourier Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized phase preconditioning followed by a unitary Fourier transform and uniform frequency sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}\) be the unitary discrete Fourier transform, let \(D\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}\) be diagonal with independent entries of unit modulus and mean zero, and let \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) select \(m\) frequencies uniformly without replacement. A subsampled randomized Fourier sketch is
\[
S=\sqrt{\frac{n}{m}}RFD.
\]
For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{C}^n\), uniform sampling and unitarity yield \(\mathbb E_R\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\), conditional on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SRFT randomizes phases, applies the unitary Fourier transform, samples frequencies uniformly, and rescales to preserve norm in expectation.
assumptions_latex: The diagonal entries of \(D\) are independent, mean-zero, and unit-modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\sqrt{n/m}RFD\) and \(\mathbb E_R\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover subsampled Fourier sketches.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SRFT construction is mathematically coherent and fits the definition leaf, but it lacks a supporting citation and locator.

children.title: CountSketch Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Sparse embeddings based on CountSketch structure.

knowledge_statements.title: CountSketch Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-nonzero-per-column sparse embedding generated by hashing coordinates into signed buckets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose independently a hash map \(h:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}\), uniform on the buckets, and signs \(\sigma_j\in\{-1,1\}\) with equal probabilities. The CountSketch matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is defined by
\[
S_{ij}=\sigma_j\mathbf 1\{h(j)=i\}.
\]
Thus every column contains exactly one nonzero entry, and for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
(Sx)_i=\sum_{j:h(j)=i}\sigma_jx_j.
\]
Pairwise-independent hashing and signs suffice for the identity \(\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CountSketch hashes each coordinate into one bucket with a random sign, producing a matrix with exactly one nonzero per column.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma_j\) are unbiased random signs independent of the hash values.
Pairwise independence is assumed for the expectation identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{ij}=\sigma_j\mathbf 1\{h(j)=i\}\) and \(\mathbb E\lVert Sx\rVert_2^2=\lVert x\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: Random sign attached to coordinate j.

review_flags: The supplied inventory locators do not cover CountSketch embeddings.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The CountSketch matrix definition is standard, but the opening independence language and later pairwise-independence claim should be matched to an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Feature-Hashing Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Hash-based sparse embeddings beyond the canonical CountSketch presentation.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Hashing Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed one-bucket-per-feature embedding for finite-dimensional vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:[d]\to[m]\) be a hash function and let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\in\{-1,1\}\) be signs. The feature-hashing matrix is \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\) defined by \(S_{ij}=\xi_j\) when \(i=h(j)\), and \(S_{ij}=0\) otherwise. Thus every column has exactly one nonzero entry, and for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\),
\[
(Sx)_i=\sum_{j:h(j)=i}\xi_jx_j,\qquad i\in[m].
\]
A randomized feature-hashing embedding draws \(h\) and the signs from specified distributions, commonly with uniform hash locations and independent symmetric signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feature hashing sends each signed coordinate to one bucket, so coordinates assigned to the same bucket are summed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{ij}=\xi_j\mathbf{1}_{\{h(j)=i\}}\) and \((Sx)_i=\sum_{j:h(j)=i}\xi_jx_j\).

notation.meaning: Hash function assigning input coordinates to output buckets.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: signed one-sparse hashing construction is standard but uncited

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, matches the feature-hashing leaf, and uses an appropriate content kind, but source_refs is empty. The standard-field rationale does not satisfy the requirement for an inspectable citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Collision Regimes
children.top_down_role: Embedding-quality effects caused by hash collisions and bucket congestion.

knowledge_statements.title: Collision Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collision descriptors for one-bucket-per-column hash embeddings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a hash function \(h:[d]\to[m]\), define the bucket load \(L_i=|\{j:h(j)=i\}|\), maximum load \(L_{\max}=\max_{i\in[m]}L_i\), and collision count
\[
C(h)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\binom{L_i}{2}=|\{\{j,k\}:j<k,\ h(j)=h(k)\}|.
\]
A collision-free regime on an active coordinate set \(T\subseteq[d]\) means that \(h|_T\) is injective. A bounded-collision regime with parameter \(q\in\mathbb{N}\) means \(\max_i|T\cap h^{-1}(i)|\le q\). These predicates distinguish exact isolation from controlled aggregation of active coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Collision regimes classify a hash map by bucket loads or colliding pairs, optionally restricted to coordinates active in the optimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Collision-free means \(h|_T\) is injective; bounded collision means \(\max_i|T\cap h^{-1}(i)|\le q\).

notation.meaning: Number of coordinates assigned to bucket \(i\).
Number of unordered coordinate pairs that collide.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bucket-load predicates directly formalize hashing collisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bucket-load, collision-count, collision-free, and bounded-collision predicates are internally consistent and condition is an appropriate content kind. An inspectable source is required to establish that these particular predicates and terminology represent the intended collision regimes in this leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Sign Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-sparse random sign matrix with normalized nonzero entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(1\le s\le m\). A sparse sign embedding is a random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\) constructed by choosing, for every column \(j\), a support \(H_j\subseteq[m]\) of cardinality \(s\) and signs \(\xi_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}\) for \(i\in H_j\), then setting
\[
S_{ij}=\begin{cases}\xi_{ij}/\sqrt{s},&i\in H_j,\\0,&i\notin H_j.\end{cases}
\]
The support and sign laws are part of the embedding specification. Under symmetric signs, every fixed column satisfies \(\|Se_j\|_2=1\), and distinct coordinates interact only through overlaps of their sampled supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each input coordinate is copied with random signs into a small number of output rows and normalized by the square root of that sparsity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each column of \(S\) has exactly \(s\) nonzeros of magnitude \(s^{-1/2}\), hence \(\|Se_j\|_2=1\).

notation.meaning: Number of nonzero entries per column.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized column-sparse sign construction is standard but uncited

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized column-sparse sign construction is precise, and the unit column norm follows from the stated support cardinality. Definition fits the terminal container, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting the construction and naming convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Sampling Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: With-replacement uniform row sampling with unbiased norm scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\), choose indices \(i_1,\ldots,i_r\) independently and uniformly from \([n]\), and define \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n}\) by
\[
S_{k,:}=\sqrt{\frac{n}{r}}\,e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T},\qquad k\in[r].
\]
Then \(SA\) consists of the sampled rows of \(A\), each scaled by \(\sqrt{n/r}\). For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), the scaling gives
\[
\mathbb{E}\|SAx\|_2^2=\|Ax\|_2^2.
\]
Sampling without replacement is a distinct uniform-sampling convention and requires its corresponding normalization and dependence model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform sampling sketch selects rows uniformly and rescales them so the squared norm of every fixed sketched product is unbiased.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) is fixed independently of the sampled indices
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{k,:}=\sqrt{n/r}\,e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\mathbb{E}\|SAx\|_2^2=\|Ax\|_2^2\).

notation.meaning: Row index drawn for sketch row \(k\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unbiased with-replacement uniform sampling formula follows directly from the construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The with-replacement construction, scaling, and fixed-vector unbiasedness claim are mathematically consistent, and definition fits the leaf. The claim remains unsupported because source_refs is empty and the local inventory supplies no sketch-specific citation.

children.title: Importance-Sampling Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sampling sketches weighted by problem-specific importance measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampling Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-weighted row sampling with inverse-probability rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\) and let \(p\in(0,1]^n\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\). Draw \(i_1,\ldots,i_r\) independently with \(\mathbb{P}(i_k=i)=p_i\), and set
\[
S_{k,:}=\frac{e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{r p_{i_k}}},\qquad k\in[r].
\]
The probabilities are importance weights chosen from row information relevant to the target computation. For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\),
\[
\mathbb{E}\|SAx\|_2^2=\sum_{i=1}^n\|e_i^{\mathsf T}Ax\|_2^2=\|Ax\|_2^2.
\]
Thus inverse-probability scaling corrects the nonuniform sampling bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rows are sampled with prescribed importance probabilities and divided by the square root of their sampling probabilities, yielding an unbiased squared norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{k,:}=e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt{r p_{i_k}}\) and \(\mathbb{E}\|SAx\|_2^2=\|Ax\|_2^2\) for fixed \(x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inverse-probability sampling and unbiasedness are standard but uncited

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-probability row-sampling definition and unbiased squared-norm identity are correctly scoped to independent with-replacement draws. Definition is the correct role, but an authoritative source with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: Leverage-Score Sampling Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sampling sketches driven by row, column, or subspace leverage scores.

knowledge_statements.title: Leverage-Score Sampling Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row sampling proportional to statistical leverage scores of a matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\) have rank \(\rho\ge1\), with rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). Its row leverage scores are
\[
\tau_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{\dagger}a_i,
\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n\tau_i=\rho.
\]
A leverage-score sampling sketch draws \(i_1,\ldots,i_r\) independently with \(p_i=\tau_i/\rho\) for positive-score rows and sets \(S_{k,:}=e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt{r p_{i_k}}\). Rows with \(\tau_i=0\) lie outside the column-space energy and need not be sampled. The resulting sketch preferentially samples rows having greater influence on \(\operatorname{range}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This sketch samples each row in proportion to its leverage score and applies inverse-probability scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i=\tau_i/\rho\), where \(\tau_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{\dagger}a_i\), and \(S_{k,:}=e_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt{r p_{i_k}}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: leverage-score definition and proportional sampling rule are standard but uncited

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leverage-score formula, score sum, treatment of zero-score rows, and proportional sampling rule are coherent for a rank-positive finite matrix. Definition fits the leaf, but source_refs is empty and the supplied inventory does not support this specialized construction.

children.title: Approximate-Score Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quality and cost tradeoffs when sampling scores are estimated.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Score Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative upper approximations used in leverage-based sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_n\) be exact nonnegative row scores and let \(\widetilde\tau_1,\ldots,\widetilde\tau_n\) be computable surrogates. An \(\alpha\)-approximate upper-score regime, with \(\alpha\ge1\), satisfies
\[
\tau_i\le\widetilde\tau_i\le\alpha\tau_i
\]
for every \(i\) with \(\tau_i>0\), and \(\widetilde\tau_i=0\) when \(\tau_i=0\). Sampling uses \(p_i=\widetilde\tau_i/\sum_j\widetilde\tau_j\). Consequently,
\[
p_i\ge\frac{\tau_i}{\alpha\sum_j\tau_j}.
\]
Thus every row receives at least a \(1/\alpha\) fraction of its exact score-proportional probability, identifying the oversampling loss caused by approximate scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate upper scores within factor alpha give every row at least one over alpha of its exact score-proportional sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(p_i=\widetilde\tau_i/\sum_j\widetilde\tau_j\), one has \(p_i\ge\tau_i/(\alpha\sum_j\tau_j)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: probability lower bound follows algebraically from the stated approximation regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated multiplicative upper-score regime implies the displayed probability lower bound, and condition is an appropriate content kind. A source is still needed to support this particular approximation convention and its interpretation as the intended approximate-score regime.

children.title: Sketch Lifecycle Regimes
children.top_down_role: How sketches persist, refresh, or depend on the optimization history.

children.title: One-Shot Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches used for a single reduced model or decision.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Shot Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sketch drawn for one update or one sketched subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an iterative method with filtration \((\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge0}\), where \(\mathcal{F}_t\) contains all information available before iteration \(t\). A sketch \(S_t\) is one-shot if it is drawn according to a prescribed conditional law given \(\mathcal{F}_t\), used to form exactly one update or solve exactly one sketched subproblem at iteration \(t\), and then discarded. No later update may query \(S_t\) or a stored quantity whose purpose is to reuse that same sketch realization. The definition concerns sketch lifecycle; it does not itself require \(S_t\) to be independent of \(\mathcal{F}_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-shot sketch is drawn, used for one iteration or subproblem, and discarded without reuse in later updates.
assumptions_latex: \(S_t\) is sampled before the iteration-\(t\) update
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The realization \(S_t\) affects only the iteration-\(t\) sketched computation and is not reused at later iterations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the lifecycle leaf and distinguishes one-use lifecycle from independence. However, the prohibition on later use of stored derived quantities introduces a substantive boundary whose exact scope is not standard enough to validate without a specific source.

children.title: Reused Sketches
children.top_down_role: Fixed sketches reused across multiple models or iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reused Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single sketch realization used in multiple algorithmic updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For update times in an index set \(T\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) with \(|T|\ge2\), a reused-sketch regime draws one random matrix \(S\) and employs that same realization in every sketched computation indexed by \(t\in T\). Equivalently, \(S_t=S\) for all \(t\in T\). Although \(S\) may be independent of the initial state, iterates generated after its first use generally have the form \(x_t=\Phi_t(S,\zeta_0,\ldots,\zeta_{t-1})\), so later iterates and the reused sketch need not be independent. Reuse may reduce sketch-construction cost, but its dependence structure must be represented in convergence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reused-sketch method applies the same random matrix to at least two updates, making later iterates potentially dependent on that matrix.
assumptions_latex: One realization \(S\) is available throughout the indexed updates
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t=S\) for every \(t\in T\), and later iterates may be measurable functions of \(S\).

notation.meaning: Set of update indices sharing the sketch.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality of sketch realizations directly defines reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Using one realization at multiple update times precisely describes sketch reuse, and definition is the correct content kind. The dependence discussion is plausible but requires an inspectable source tied to reused-sketch iterative methods.

children.title: Reuse-Induced Dependence
children.top_down_role: Statistical and geometric effects produced by repeated use of one sketch.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Induced Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why fixed-vector sketch guarantees cannot automatically be reused adaptively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a random sketch \(S\) satisfy, for every deterministic \(v\in\mathbb{R}^d\),
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl(|\|Sv\|_2^2-\|v\|_2^2|\le\varepsilon\|v\|_2^2\bigr)\ge1-\delta.
\]
If the same \(S\) is reused and an iterate or query \(v_t\) is computed from earlier outputs involving \(S\), then \(v_t\) is generally \(\sigma(S)\)-dependent. The displayed fixed-vector guarantee cannot be applied conditionally to \(v_t\) without an additional uniform embedding event, a valid conditional guarantee, or an argument controlling adaptive dependence. Treating \(v_t\) as independent of \(S\) marks the failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing a sketch can make future queries depend on it, so a guarantee for fixed independent vectors does not automatically cover those queries.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) obeys only the displayed fixed-vector probability guarantee
\(v_t\) is computed using earlier quantities derived from the same \(S\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed-vector guarantee alone does not justify the same probability claim for the \(S\)-dependent query \(v_t\).

notation.meaning: Sigma-algebra generated by the sketch realization.
Failure-probability bound for a fixed vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise probability bounds do not imply conditional bounds for data-dependent queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly identifies a failure boundary: a pointwise fixed-vector guarantee cannot automatically be substituted for a guarantee on an S-dependent query. The content kind is appropriate, but this nontrivial limitation and its listed remedies require authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Independently Resampled Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh sketch randomness independent of the pre-update history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge0}\) be the history before each update. An independently resampled sketch regime requires a sequence \((S_t)_{t\ge0}\) such that \(S_t\) has the prescribed sketch distribution and
\[
S_t\ \text{is independent of }\mathcal{F}_t
\]
for every \(t\). In particular, when \(\mathcal{F}_t\) contains \(S_0,\ldots,S_{t-1}\), the sketches are mutually independent. Consequently, any iterate \(x_t\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{F}_t\) is independent of \(S_t\), permitting fixed-input sketch guarantees to be applied conditionally at iteration \(t\), provided their other hypotheses hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iteration a fresh sketch is drawn independently of all prior iterates and sketches, enabling conditional use of fixed-input guarantees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditionally on \(\mathcal{F}_t\), \(S_t\) retains its prescribed law and is independent of \(x_t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: independence from the pre-update filtration formalizes fresh resampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Independence of each sketch from the pre-update filtration is a coherent condition for fresh resampling and gives the stated conditional-law consequence. The exact lifecycle condition and its use with fixed-input guarantees need a specific stochastic-optimization or sketching citation.

children.title: Adaptive Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketch distributions or dimensions selected from current optimization information.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sketch distributions selected from the observed optimization history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge0}\) be the pre-update history. A sketch sequence \((S_t)_{t\ge0}\) is adaptive if its conditional distribution is selected through an \(\mathcal{F}_t\)-measurable probability kernel \(K_t\):
\[
\mathbb{P}(S_t\in B\mid\mathcal{F}_t)=K_t(B;\mathcal{F}_t)
\]
for every measurable set \(B\). Thus sketch dimensions, sampling probabilities, sparsity, or distribution families may depend on previous iterates, oracle responses, and sketch outcomes. Conditional on \(\mathcal{F}_t\), fresh randomness used to sample from \(K_t\) may remain independent, but the unconditional sketch law can vary with the realized history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive sketch is sampled from a distribution chosen measurably from the optimization history, possibly changing size, sparsity, or sampling probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional sketch law satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(S_t\in B\mid\mathcal{F}_t)=K_t(B;\mathcal{F}_t)\) for every measurable \(B\).

notation.meaning: History-dependent probability kernel for the next sketch.
Measurable set of admissible sketch matrices.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A history-measurable probability kernel is a plausible formal definition of an adaptive sketch law, and definition fits the leaf. Validation requires a source and an explicit measurable space for the admissible sketches so that the kernel and measurable sets B are well-defined.

children.title: History-Dependent Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches whose construction depends on prior iterates, models, or outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Dependent Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines sketches measurable with respect to the optimization history available before their use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be the current iterate and let \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(x_0,g_0,S_0,\ldots,x_t,g_t)\) denote the information available before the next sketch is applied. A random matrix \(S_t\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q_t}\) is a history-dependent sketch if its conditional law is an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable probability kernel: for every Borel set \(B\), the map \(\omega\mapsto\mathbb P(S_t\in B\mid\mathcal F_t)(\omega)\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. Thus \(S_t\) may depend on past iterates, oracle outputs, and sketches, while any additional random seed used at time \(t\) is sampled conditionally on \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-dependent sketch may use all information revealed before iteration t, with any fresh randomness described by a conditional distribution measurable with respect to that history.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,g_t\), and earlier sketches are random elements on a common probability space.
\(S_t\) takes values in the Borel space \(\mathbb R^{n\times q_t}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\) is history-dependent exactly when its conditional distribution given \(\mathcal F_t\) is an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable probability kernel.

notation.meaning: information available before the time-t sketch is applied

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports adaptive history-dependent sketch kernels.
Exact filtration convention requires source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable source is supplied. Moreover, measurability of a regular conditional law with respect to the conditioning sigma-algebra is automatic and therefore does not by itself distinguish history-dependent sketches. A source-backed definition must clarify whether the sketch, its selection rule, or its conditional kernel is allowed to depend nontrivially on the pre-sketch history.

children.title: Selection-Bias Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity risks introduced by data-dependent or trajectory-dependent sketch selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Bias Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when fixed-sketch concentration cannot be reused after data-dependent sketch selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{S_j\}_{j=1}^M\) be candidate sketches and let \(E_j\) be a claimed accuracy event satisfying \(\mathbb P(E_j)\geq1-\delta\) for each fixed index \(j\). If an index \(J\) is selected using information that also determines the events \(E_j\), the fixed-index bounds alone do not imply \(\mathbb P(E_J)\geq1-\delta\). A valid selected-sketch guarantee requires, for example, conditional control \(\mathbb P(E_j^c\mid J=j)\leq\delta\) for every selected value, independence of \(J\) from the validation randomness, or simultaneous control \(\mathbb P(\bigcap_{j=1}^M E_j)\geq1-\delta\). Without such control, selection can systematically choose a failing sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A guarantee for every fixed sketch need not survive adaptive selection; conditional, independent-validation, or simultaneous control is required to prevent selection bias.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The marginal fixed-index bounds do not generally entail \(\mathbb P(E_J)\geq1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: accuracy event for candidate sketch j

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports post-selection sketch guarantees.
A source is needed for the intended adaptive-selection formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and the listed remedies are mathematically plausible, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. However, no source or locator supports the intended post-selection formulation. Source confirmation should also state that conditional bounds are required only for indices with positive selection probability.

children.title: Streaming Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches maintained as data arrive through a stream.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a one-pass stateful sketch of sequentially arriving optimization data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let data items \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\) arrive sequentially from a measurable space \(\mathcal A\). A streaming sketch with memory budget \(m\) consists of a state space \(\mathcal Z_m\), an initial state \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_m\), and update maps \(U_i:\mathcal Z_m\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z_m\) such that \(z_i=U_i(z_{i-1},a_i)\). Each item is accessed only when it arrives, and the persistent state has storage at most \(m\) machine words. A subspace estimate is produced as \(Q=R(z_N)\), where \(R\) is a readout map and the columns of \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) span the retained optimization subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A streaming sketch updates a bounded-memory state as data arrive once in order, then reads a low-dimensional optimization subspace from the final state.
assumptions_latex: The stream order and machine-word storage model are fixed.
Each \(a_i\) is unavailable after its update unless encoded in \(z_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=R(z_N)\) is a one-pass, bounded-memory subspace summary of the stream.

notation.meaning: persistent sketch state after item i
readout basis for the retained subspace

review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses streaming subspace sketches.
The intended access and memory model needs direct source support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the appropriate content kind, but no cited source fixes the one-pass access model, stream ordering, or machine-word memory convention. These conventions materially determine what counts as a streaming sketch.

children.title: Single-View Sketches
children.top_down_role: Sketches constructed with only one complete view of the data.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-View Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines subspace construction from one simultaneous access to an input operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and choose test matrices \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) and \(\Psi\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times m}\) before accessing \(A\). A single-view sketch observes only the pair \(Y=A\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi A\), formed during the same pass over the entries or blocks of \(A\). Its output subspace \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) must be measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\Omega,\Psi,Y,W)\); it may not subsequently multiply \(A\) or \(A^{\mathsf T}\) by a vector chosen from \(Y\) or \(W\). A standard output is \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{range}(Q)\), where \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-view method fixes its probes beforehand, forms all sketches in one access to the input, and constructs its subspace without later adaptive products with the input.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) are chosen independently of values revealed while reading \(A\).
The products \(A\Omega\) and \(\Psi A\) can be accumulated in one pass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\mathcal U\) depends only on the preselected probes and their simultaneously collected sketches.

notation.meaning: right and left sketches collected in one view
orthonormal basis obtained from the range sketch

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports the two-sided single-view model.
A randomized linear-algebra source is required to certify this convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the leaf and the dimensions are consistent, but the two-sided simultaneous-sketch convention and prohibition on subsequent adaptive products require a randomized linear-algebra source with a specific locator.

children.title: Limited-Pass Constraints
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and storage consequences of restricted data access.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Pass Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal access restriction for sketches allowed only a prescribed number of data passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer \(p\geq1\) and an input \(A\) stored as an ordered sequence of blocks. A sketching procedure satisfies the \(p\)-pass constraint if its execution can be partitioned into at most \(p\) complete sequential scans of those blocks. During a scan it may update a persistent state of at most \(m\) machine words; between scans it may retain only that state and predeclared auxiliary randomness. Every query involving \(A\) must be computable from the block currently being scanned and the current state. In particular, an adaptively chosen product requiring a new traversal of \(A\) consumes an additional pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A p-pass method may scan the input at most p times, retains only bounded state between scans, and counts every new adaptive traversal as another pass.
assumptions_latex: The block order, persistent-memory budget \(m\), and pass-counting convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is feasible in the limited-pass model precisely when it obeys the stated scan, state, and query restrictions.

notation.meaning: maximum number of complete input scans

review_flags: The supplied inventory has no limited-pass sketching source.
Pass and persistent-memory conventions require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for this leaf. No source establishes the particular scan, persistent-state, auxiliary-randomness, and pass-counting conventions, so the exact limited-pass model remains unsupported.

knowledge_statements.title: Isotropic Random Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rotationally invariant random subspaces and their projector expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(1\leq q\leq n\), a random \(q\)-dimensional subspace \(\mathcal U\) of \(\mathbb R^n\) is isotropic if \(R\mathcal U\) has the same distribution as \(\mathcal U\) for every orthogonal matrix \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Equivalently, \(\mathcal U\) has the Haar probability law on the Grassmannian \(\operatorname{Gr}(q,n)\). If \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\mathcal U\) and \(P=QQ^{\mathsf T}\), then rotational invariance and \(\operatorname{tr}(P)=q\) give \(\mathbb E[P]=(q/n)I_n\), hence \(\mathbb E\|Q^{\mathsf T}v\|_2^2=(q/n)\|v\|_2^2\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isotropic random q-subspace is rotation invariant; on average its projector captures the fraction q/n of every vector’s squared norm.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is an orthonormal basis of \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[QQ^{\mathsf T}]=(q/n)I_n\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q^{\mathsf T}v\|_2^2=(q/n)\|v\|_2^2\) for all \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Grassmannian of q-dimensional subspaces of Euclidean n-space
orthonormal basis matrix for the random subspace
orthogonal projector onto the random subspace

review_flags: The statement is standard, but no supplied locator directly covers Haar-distributed Grassmannian subspaces.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotational-invariance definition and projector expectation are standard and internally consistent, and definition is acceptable for this topic container. Nevertheless, no source with an inspectable locator is supplied for either the Haar characterization or the expectation identity.

children.title: Coordinate Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces based on individual coordinate directions without duplicating coordinate-method algorithms.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines subspaces spanned by selected standard coordinate directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) be the standard basis of \(\mathbb R^n\). For an index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the coordinate subspace associated with \(I\) is \(\mathcal U_I=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\}\). Its basis matrix is \(S_I=[e_i]_{i\in I}\), its orthogonal projector is \(P_I=S_IS_I^{\mathsf T}\), and the projected vector satisfies \((P_Ix)_i=x_i\) for \(i\in I\) and \((P_Ix)_i=0\) otherwise. A first-order step restricted to \(\mathcal U_I\) changes only coordinates indexed by \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate subspace is spanned by selected standard basis vectors; projection keeps exactly those coordinates, and a restricted step changes no others.
assumptions_latex: \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) is the standard orthonormal basis of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_I=\operatorname{range}(S_I)\) and \(P_I=S_IS_I^{\mathsf T}\) retains exactly the coordinates in \(I\).

notation.meaning: matrix of selected standard basis vectors

A step \(d\in\mathcal U_J\) may couple all coordinates within the selected blocks but satisfies \(d_i=0\) for every \(i\notin I_J\).

children.title: Coordinate-to-Block Granularity
children.top_down_role: Subspace-quality and resource tradeoffs across coordinate grouping scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-to-Block Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders coordinate-block models by refinement of their underlying partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B_1\) and \(\mathcal B_2\) be partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(\mathcal B_1\) refining \(\mathcal B_2\), so every block of \(\mathcal B_1\) lies in a block of \(\mathcal B_2\). For any \(C\in\mathcal B_2\), the coarse block subspace \(\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in C\}\) is the orthogonal direct sum of the fine block subspaces indexed by \(B\in\mathcal B_1\) with \(B\subseteq C\). Consequently, single-coordinate granularity is the finest partition, while merging blocks enlarges each atomic admissible update subspace and permits more within-step coordinate coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition refinement formalizes granularity: fine block spaces sum to each coarse block space, while coarser blocks permit larger coupled updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(C\in\mathcal B_2\), \(\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in C\}=\bigoplus_{B\in\mathcal B_1,\,B\subseteq C}\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in B\}\).

a fine coordinate block contained in C

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Informed Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines subspaces selected measurably from current problem data rather than solely from an invariant prior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_t\) denote optimization data available when a subspace is constructed, such as sampled gradients, residuals, Jacobian products, or feature vectors. A random subspace \(\mathcal U_t\in\operatorname{Gr}(q_t,n)\) is data-informed if there exist auxiliary randomness \(\xi_t\), independent of \(D_t\), and a measurable map \(\Phi_t\) such that \(\mathcal U_t=\Phi_t(D_t,\xi_t)\), and the conditional law of \(\mathcal U_t\) is not constant in \(D_t\). Equivalently, some measurable set \(B\subseteq\operatorname{Gr}(q_t,n)\) has \(\mathbb P(\mathcal U_t\in B\mid D_t)\) depending nontrivially on \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A data-informed subspace is selected from observed optimization data, possibly with independent auxiliary randomness, and its conditional distribution genuinely changes with those data.
assumptions_latex: \(D_t\) and \(\xi_t\) are random elements on a common probability space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_t\) is data-informed when its conditional distribution given \(D_t\) depends nontrivially on \(D_t\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary random seed independent of the data

review_flags: No supplied locator defines data-informed subspace generation.

children.title: History-Enriched Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Subspaces enlarged using information retained from prior optimization states.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Enriched Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a current trial subspace augmented by directions retained from optimization history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_t\in\mathbb R^{n\times q_t}\) contain newly generated trial directions and let \(H_t\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_t}\) contain directions computed before iteration \(t\), such as previous steps or gradients. The history-enriched subspace is \(\mathcal U_t=\operatorname{range}([V_t\ H_t])\). If \(Q_t=\operatorname{orth}([V_t\ H_t])\), then \(\mathcal U_t=\operatorname{range}(Q_t)\), \(\operatorname{range}(V_t)\subseteq\mathcal U_t\), and \(\operatorname{range}(H_t)\subseteq\mathcal U_t\). Linear dependence is removed by orthogonalization, so \(\dim(\mathcal U_t)=\operatorname{rank}([V_t\ H_t])\leq q_t+r_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-enriched subspace spans both new trial directions and retained past directions, with redundant directions removed by orthogonalization.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(H_t\) are available before the iteration-t subspace step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_t=\operatorname{range}([V_t\ H_t])\) contains both constituent ranges and has dimension \(\operatorname{rank}([V_t\ H_t])\).

notation.meaning: matrix of newly generated trial directions
orthonormal basis of the enriched subspace

Examples of admissible historical directions need source confirmation.

children.title: Recycled Subspaces

knowledge_statements.title: Recycled Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reuse of a previously computed subspace or a selected portion of it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{t-1}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning the previously retained subspace, and let \(C_t\in\mathbb R^{r\times s_t}\) be chosen before the current subspace solve. A recycled subspace is \(\mathcal R_t=\operatorname{range}(Q_{t-1}C_t)\), possibly with \(C_t=I_r\) for full reuse. If \(Z_t=\operatorname{orth}(Q_{t-1}C_t)\), then \(\mathcal R_t=\operatorname{range}(Z_t)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q_{t-1})\). Recycling differs from enrichment: it specifies the carried-over component itself, which may subsequently be combined with newly generated directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recycled subspace reuses all or a selected part of an earlier basis; it is contained in the previously retained subspace and may later be augmented.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t\) is available before the current reduced subproblem is solved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_t=\operatorname{range}(Q_{t-1}C_t)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q_{t-1})\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis retained from a previous iteration
coefficient or selection matrix for reuse

children.title: Staleness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where retained directions cease to represent current problem geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Staleness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies when a recycled subspace can cease to represent the current gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(S_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a subspace constructed at \(x_j\), and let \(P_j\) be its orthogonal projector. If \(\|(I-P_j)\nabla f(x_j)\|\leq \varepsilon_j\), then at a later point \(x_k\), \[\|(I-P_j)\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq \varepsilon_j+L\|x_k-x_j\|.\] Hence a required capture tolerance \(\tau\) is guaranteed only while \(\varepsilon_j+L\|x_k-x_j\|\leq\tau\). Beyond this boundary the original capture certificate alone gives no \(\tau\)-adequacy guarantee, even though the recycled subspace may remain useful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recycled subspace retains its certified gradient capture only while iterate drift, scaled by gradient Lipschitzness, stays within the remaining tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P_j\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(S_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(I-P_j)\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_j+L\|x_k-x_j\|\), with certified tolerance \(\tau\) only inside the stated boundary.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the subspace built at iteration j.

children.title: Krylov-Generated Subspaces
