knowledge_statements.title: Krylov-Generated Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear and quadratic first-order interface using a residual-generated Krylov space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a nonzero residual or gradient \(r\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and an integer \(m\geq1\), the order-\(m\) Krylov-generated subspace is \[\mathcal{K}_m(H,r)=\operatorname{span}\{r,Hr,\ldots,H^{m-1}r\}.\] In a quadratic model \(q(s)=q(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), one takes \(r=g\) or \(r=-g\) and restricts the step to \(s\in\mathcal{K}_m(H,r)\). More generally, products with \(H\) may be supplied by a Hessian-vector or linear-operator oracle without forming \(H\) explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive applications of a symmetric linear operator to a gradient or residual span the Krylov subspace in which a reduced step is computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{K}_m(H,r)=\operatorname{span}\{H^jr:0\leq j<m\}\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric model Hessian or linear operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-Direction Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative condition ensuring that a subspace contains a sufficiently aligned descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable at \(x\), let \(g=\nabla f(x)\neq0\), and let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a linear subspace. For \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), the subspace has \(\gamma\)-descent-direction coverage at \(x\) when there exists \(d\in S\setminus\{0\}\) such that \[-g^{\mathsf T}d\geq\gamma\|g\|\|d\|.\] Equivalently, \(\|P_Sg\|\geq\gamma\|g\|\), where \(P_S\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(S\). When the condition holds, \(d=-P_Sg\) is a descent direction unless \(g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace covers descent when it contains a direction whose angle with the negative gradient has cosine at least the prescribed threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists d\in S\setminus\{0\}:-g^{\mathsf T}d\geq\gamma\|g\|\|d\|\), equivalently \(\|P_Sg\|\geq\gamma\|g\|\).

children.title: Constraint-Space Coverage
children.top_down_role: Coverage of directions associated with the active constraint geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Space Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coverage of attainable linearized equality-constraint changes by a sampled subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the linearized equality constraints at \(x\) be \(Ad=-c\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and let \(S=\operatorname{range}(U)\) for \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\). The subspace has exact constraint-space coverage when \[\operatorname{range}(AU)=\operatorname{range}(A).\] Equivalently, for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there exists \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(AUz=Ad\). Consequently, whenever \(Ad=-c\) is consistent, the reduced equation \(AUz=-c\) is also consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact constraint-space coverage means that subspace directions can reproduce every linearized constraint change attainable in the full space, so every consistent full-space correction has a reduced-space correction.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is the equality-constraint Jacobian at the current point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(AU)=\operatorname{range}(A)\), so consistency of \(Ad=-c\) implies consistency of \(AUz=-c\).

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns generate the sampled subspace.
Current equality-constraint residual appearing in the linearized correction equation.

children.title: Tangent-Space Coverage
children.top_down_role: Coverage of directions lying within local tangent geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Space Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A uniform projection condition for representing linearized feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{F}=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(y)=0\}\), where \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable at \(x\in\mathcal{F}\), and let \(J=\nabla c(x)\) have full row rank. Then the tangent space is \(T_x=\ker J\). For a linear subspace \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its orthogonal projector \(P_S\), and \(\eta\in[0,1]\), say that \(S\) has \(\eta\)-tangent-space coverage at \(x\) when \[\inf_{d\in T_x\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\|P_Sd\|}{\|d\|}\geq\eta.\] Equivalently, the smallest gain of the restricted map \(P_S|_{T_x}:T_x\to S\) is at least \(\eta\). Exact coverage corresponds to \(\eta=1\), in which case \(T_x\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent-space coverage uniformly lower-bounds the fraction of every linearized feasible direction retained by projection onto the sampled subspace. Exact coverage means that the sampled subspace contains the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{d\in\ker J\setminus\{0\}}\|P_Sd\|/\|d\|\geq\eta\); if \(\eta=1\), then \(\ker J\subseteq S\).

notation.meaning: Linearized tangent space ker J at the feasible point x.
Euclidean orthogonal projector onto the sampled subspace.

children.title: Feasible-Direction Transfer
children.top_down_role: How sampled-space coverage supports useful directions in the feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers reduced null-space coordinates into feasible full-space directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be a linearized equality-constraint Jacobian and let \(S=\operatorname{range}(U)\), with \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) of full column rank. Define the reduced tangent-coordinate space by \(Z=\ker(JU)\). Then every \(z\in Z\) transfers to the full-space direction \(d=Uz\in S\cap\ker J\). Conversely, every \(d\in S\cap\ker J\) has a unique coordinate \(z\in Z\) satisfying \(d=Uz\). Thus \[U(\ker(JU))=S\cap\ker J,\] and reduced null-space feasibility is exactly equivalent to full-space linearized feasibility within \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subspace basis maps reduced null-space vectors bijectively onto the feasible directions lying in the sampled subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is a linearized equality-constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(\ker(JU))=\operatorname{range}(U)\cap\ker J\), with unique reduced coordinates.

notation.meaning: Injective coordinate map for the sampled subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The range-kernel identity and uniqueness under full column rank are correct, and property is an appropriate role for this transfer statement. No inspectable source is supplied for this nontrivial constrained-subspace formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Fidelity in Sampled Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully linear first-order fidelity restricted to sampled displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(S=\operatorname{range}(U)\), and let \(m:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\) model \(f(x+Us)\) on \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\). The model is \((\kappa_f,\kappa_g)\)-fully linear on the sampled ball when, for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^p\) with \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\), \[|f(x+Us)-m(s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta^2,\qquad \|U^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x+Us)-\nabla m(s)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta.\] These inequalities control function-value error and projected-gradient error only along sampled displacements; they make no claim about gradient components orthogonal to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled-space model is fully linear when its value error is quadratic and its projected-gradient error is linear in the sampling radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are differentiable on their respective sampled balls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed value and projected-gradient error bounds hold uniformly for \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the sampled subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated sampled-coordinate fully linear condition is coherent when U has orthonormal columns, and condition fits the leaf. A source is required for the particular projected-gradient formulation, radius normalization, and constants.

children.title: Subspace Coordinate-Metric Representation System
children.top_down_role: Coordinate representations and metrics used to express reduced models.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal-Basis Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean coordinate representation of a linear subspace using an orthonormal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) have dimension \(p\), and let \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) satisfy \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_p\) and \(\operatorname{range}(Q)=S\). Every \(d\in S\) has the unique representation \(d=Qz\), where \(z=Q^{\mathsf T}d\), and \(\|d\|_2=\|z\|_2\). The Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(S\) is \(P_S=QQ^{\mathsf T}\). Consequently, for any \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the subspace gradient coordinates are \(Q^{\mathsf T}g\), while its ambient projected gradient is \(QQ^{\mathsf T}g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal basis gives unique, norm-preserving subspace coordinates and represents the orthogonal projector as the basis times its transpose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=Q(Q^{\mathsf T}d)\) for \(d\in S\), \(\|d\|_2=\|Q^{\mathsf T}d\|_2\), and \(P_S=QQ^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: Matrix with orthonormal columns spanning S.
Euclidean coordinates of a subspace vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonorthogonal Sketch Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates and Euclidean projection for a full-rank, nonorthogonal sketch basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) have full column rank and let \(S=\operatorname{range}(U)\). Every \(d\in S\) has unique coordinates \(z=(U^{\mathsf T}U)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}d\) with \(d=Uz\). The coordinate Gram matrix is \(G=U^{\mathsf T}U\succ0\), so \(\|Uz\|_2^2=z^{\mathsf T}Gz\). The Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(S\) is \[P_S=U(U^{\mathsf T}U)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}.\] Thus \(U^{\mathsf T}g\) is a covector of directional derivatives, whereas \(G^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}g\) gives the coordinates of the projected ambient gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonorthogonal basis requires its Gram matrix to recover coordinates, norms, and the Euclidean orthogonal projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=U^{\mathsf T}U\succ0\), \(P_S=UG^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\|Uz\|_2^2=z^{\mathsf T}Gz\).

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-mode adequacy for a random sampled subspace at a fixed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a random linear subspace of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(P_S\) be its orthogonal projector, and let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be fixed conditional on the information available before sampling \(S\). Define \(q(S,g)=\|P_Sg\|^2/\|g\|^2\) for \(g\neq0\), and \(q(S,0)=1\). The sampling rule has expected gradient-capture quality at least \(\rho\in[0,1]\) when \[\mathbb{E}[q(S,g)\mid\mathcal{F}]\geq\rho.\] Equivalently, for \(g\neq0\), \(\mathbb{E}[\|P_Sg\|^2\mid\mathcal{F}]\geq\rho\|g\|^2\). This expectation statement alone supplies no per-sample or high-probability lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected quality lower-bounds the average fraction of squared gradient norm captured by the random subspace, conditional on the pre-sampling history.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is sampled after conditioning on the history \(\mathcal{F}\).
\(P_S\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\|P_Sg\|^2\mid\mathcal{F}]\geq\rho\|g\|^2\) for \(g\neq0\).

notation.meaning: Information available before the subspace is sampled.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-direction quality for a random sketched subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) be random, let \(P_S\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(S)\), and fix \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) independently of \(S\). Define \(q_S(v)=\|P_Sv\|_2^2/\|v\|_2^2\) when \(v\ne0\), and \(q_S(0)=1\). For \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and \(\delta\in[0,1]\), the sketch has \((\rho,\delta)\) high-probability quality for \(v\) when \[\mathbb P\!\left(q_S(v)\ge \rho\right)\ge 1-\delta.\] The probability is taken only over the construction of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random subspace has high-probability quality when it preserves at least a specified fraction of a fixed direction’s squared norm except with probability at most delta.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a random matrix and \(v\) is fixed independently of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(q_S(v)\ge\rho)\ge1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the sketched subspace.
Fraction of squared norm captured from direction v.
Quality threshold and allowed failure probability.

children.title: Uniform Quality Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Quality assessed simultaneously over a prescribed family of states or subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Quality Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One sketch must preserve every direction in a prescribed class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) be a deterministic class of informative directions, and let \(S\) be random with orthogonal range projector \(P_S\). For \(q_S(v)=\|P_Sv\|_2^2/\|v\|_2^2\), an \((\rho,\delta)\) uniform quality guarantee on \(K\) is \[\mathbb P\!\left(\inf_{v\in K}q_S(v)\ge\rho\right)\ge1-\delta.\] Thus a single realized sketch satisfies the quality inequality simultaneously for all \(v\in K\). When \(K\) is the unit sphere of a subspace \(U\), the inner infimum is \(\inf_{v\in U,\,\|v\|_2=1}\|P_Sv\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quality means that one random sketch simultaneously captures the required norm fraction for every direction in a predetermined class.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is random and \(P_S\) is its orthogonal range projector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\inf_{v\in K}q_S(v)\ge\rho)\ge1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Prescribed class of directions requiring simultaneous preservation.
Squared-norm capture ratio for direction v.
Optional target subspace whose unit sphere forms K.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous quantifier structure is correct and the condition fits Uniform Quality Guarantees, but no source supports the exact infimum-based random-sketch formulation or its subspace specialization.

children.title: Pathwise Quality Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Quality assessed along optimization trajectories generated by the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Pathwise Quality Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional per-iteration quality along an adaptive optimization trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain the trajectory history before drawing \(S_t\), and let the informative direction \(v_t\) be \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. Suppose \(P_t\) projects onto \(\operatorname{range}(S_t)\) and \[\mathbb P\!\left(\|P_tv_t\|_2^2\ge\rho_t\|v_t\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_t\right)\ge1-\delta_t\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Then the realized trajectory satisfies every quality test with probability at least \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{t=0}^{T-1}\{\|P_tv_t\|_2^2\ge\rho_t\|v_t\|_2^2\}\right)\ge1-\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\delta_t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional quality bounds remain valid along an adaptive trajectory, and a union bound controls the probability that every iteration is good.
assumptions_latex: \(v_t\) is measurable with respect to the history \(\mathcal F_t\) available before \(S_t\) is drawn.
Each conditional quality event fails with probability at most \(\delta_t\).

notation.meaning: Information available immediately before the iteration-t sketch draw.
Orthogonal projector onto the iteration-t sketched subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adaptive-history formulation and finite-horizon union-bound conclusion are mathematically coherent and fit the pathwise container. An inspectable source is nevertheless required for the trajectory-specific conditional guarantee.

children.title: Trajectory-Level Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Dependence and coverage failures that emerge across an optimization path.

knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory-Level Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal sketch quality need not yield a horizon-independent trajectory guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(v=e_1\in\mathbb R^2\), \(\rho\in(0,1]\), and \(\delta\in(0,1)\). Independently at each iteration, choose the sketched subspace as \(\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}\) with probability \(1-\delta\) and \(\operatorname{span}\{e_2\}\) with probability \(\delta\). Each iteration obeys \(\mathbb P(\|P_tv\|_2^2\ge\rho\|v\|_2^2)=1-\delta\), but all \(T\) tests pass with probability exactly \((1-\delta)^T\). Hence marginal high-probability quality alone gives no positive guarantee uniform over an unbounded trajectory. Moreover, a guarantee for fixed \(v\) is inapplicable when \(v_t\) is selected after observing \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated marginally reliable sketches can fail somewhere with probability approaching one, and fixed-direction guarantees do not cover directions chosen after seeing the sketch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\text{all }T\text{ quality tests pass})=(1-\delta)^T\to0\) as \(T\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the iteration-t random subspace.
Standard coordinate vectors in two dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Derivative Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivatives transferred between reduced and ambient coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). If the one-sided directional derivative \(f'(x;Sd)\) exists for \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), then the restricted function \(\phi(u)=f(x+Su)\) satisfies \[\phi'(0;d)=f'(x;Sd).\] Consequently, directional-derivative information available to a subspace method is the map \(d\mapsto f'(x;Sd)\). If \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), this map has the linear representation \[f'(x;Sd)=\langle S^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x),d\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced direction corresponds to an ambient direction through the subspace matrix, and their one-sided directional derivatives are identical.
assumptions_latex: The relevant one-sided directional derivatives exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi'(0;d)=f'(x;Sd)\), with \(f'(x;Sd)=\langle S^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x),d\rangle\) in the differentiable case.

notation.meaning: One-sided directional derivative of f at x along w.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradients of a convex objective restricted to affine subspace coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Define \(\phi:\mathbb R^r\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(\phi(u)=f(x+Su)\). A restricted subgradient at \(x\) relative to \(S\) is any \(\zeta\in\mathbb R^r\) satisfying \[f(x+Su)\ge f(x)+\langle\zeta,u\rangle\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^r.\] Equivalently, \(\zeta\in\partial\phi(0)\). Every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) yields \(S^{\mathsf T}g\in\partial\phi(0)\), so \[S^{\mathsf T}\partial f(x)\subseteq\partial\phi(0).\] If \((x+\operatorname{range}S)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing\), then the convex-composition chain rule gives \[\partial\phi(0)=S^{\mathsf T}\partial f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted subgradient supports the objective along every displacement in the chosen subspace. Ambient subgradients map to restricted subgradients through the transpose of the subspace matrix, and the reverse representation holds under the stated relative-interior qualification.
assumptions_latex: The equality \(\partial\phi(0)=S^{\mathsf T}\partial f(x)\) additionally assumes \((x+\operatorname{range}S)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^{\mathsf T}\partial f(x)\subseteq\partial\phi(0)\), with equality under the stated relative-interior qualification.

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of f at x.
Restriction of f to the affine subspace x plus range(S).

e\varnothing\), then this condition is equivalent to \[0\in\partial igl(f(x+S\,\cdot)+h(x+S\,\cdot) igr)(0),\] where the smooth term is differentiated in reduced coordinates and the convex subdifferential is used for the nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected composite stationarity holds when a smooth gradient plus some convex subgradient has zero component in every selected search direction. Under the stated relative-interior qualification, this is equivalent to first-order stationarity of the reduced composite objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in S^{\mathsf T}(\nabla f(x)+\partial h(x))\), with equivalence to reduced composite stationarity under the stated qualification.

notation.meaning: Composite objective with smooth and convex nonsmooth terms.
Matrix spanning the tested search subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear First-Order Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine reduced model formed from first-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and choose \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) as available first-order information, with \(g=\nabla f(x)\) in the differentiable case or \(g\in\partial f(x)\) in the convex case. For a search matrix \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), the linear first-order subspace model is \[m_x(u)=f(x)+\langle g,Su\rangle=f(x)+\langle S^{\mathsf T}g,u\rangle,\qquad u\in\mathbb R^r.\] The model assigns the ambient trial point \(x+Su\) the affine prediction generated solely by the restricted first-order vector \(S^{\mathsf T}g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear subspace model predicts objective change by pairing the reduced step with the gradient or subgradient restricted to the search subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(g=\nabla f(x)\) when f is differentiable, or \(g\in\partial f(x)\) when f is convex.
\(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) maps reduced steps to ambient steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x(u)=f(x)+\langle S^{\mathsf T}g,u\rangle\).

notation.meaning: Gradient or selected convex subgradient at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratically Regularized First-Order Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear reduced model stabilized by positive quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) be available first-order information at \(x\). Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), let \(H\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) be symmetric positive definite, and let \(\eta>0\). The quadratically regularized first-order model is \[m_x(u)=f(x)+\langle S^{\mathsf T}g,u\rangle+\frac{1}{2\eta}\langle u,Hu\rangle,\qquad u\in\mathbb R^r.\] It has the unique unconstrained minimizer \[u^+=-\eta H^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g.\] The associated ambient step is \(Su^+\). If \(H=I_r\) and the columns of \(S\) are orthonormal, then \(Su^+=-\eta SS^{\mathsf T}g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic term makes the reduced linear model strongly convex and gives a unique preconditioned projected first-order step.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) is first-order information at \(x\).
\(H\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^+=-\eta H^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g\) uniquely minimizes \(m_x\).

children.title: Subspace Step Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Families for obtaining and accepting reduced-space steps without procedural payload.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Subspace Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solution of a positive-definite quadratic first-order model on a sampled subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an iterate \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a subspace matrix \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), the projected gradient \(g_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\), and a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\), form \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}H_ks\). The unique reduced step and lifted iterate are
\[
s_k=-H_k^{-1}g_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+S_ks_k.
\]
Equivalently, \(s_k\) is the unique solution of \(H_ks=-g_k\). Stop when a prescribed full-space or projected stationarity test is satisfied; otherwise resample or update the subspace and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a positive-definite quadratic subspace model explicitly, lift its unique reduced minimizer through the subspace matrix, and repeat until a chosen stationarity test holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=-H_k^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\) uniquely minimizes \(m_k\).

notation.meaning: matrix whose range is the current search subspace

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-definite quadratic minimization gives the displayed linear-system solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definite quadratic minimizer is mathematically correct and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the complete subspace-step interface, including lifting, stopping, and subspace resampling or updating.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Iterative Subspace Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact iterative solution of a smooth reduced model with a residual-based termination rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iterate \(x_k\), choose \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) and a differentiable reduced model \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\). Initialize \(s_{k,0}=0\) and apply a specified first-order inner method to generate \(s_{k,j+1}\) from \(s_{k,j}\). Terminate at the first index \(j_k\) satisfying
\[
\|\nabla m_k(s_{k,j_k})\|\leq \eta_k\|\nabla m_k(0)\|,
\qquad 0\leq\eta_k<1,
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+S_ks_{k,j_k}\). If no such index is reached within the inner budget, report an unsuccessful subproblem solve rather than asserting the required relative accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively solve the reduced model until its gradient norm is a prescribed fraction of the initial residual, then lift the approximate reduced step.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is differentiable on the inner iterates.
The inner method and its iteration budget are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted reduced step \(s_k=s_{k,j_k}\) satisfies \(\|\nabla m_k(s_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|\nabla m_k(0)\|\).

notation.meaning: inner iterate for outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Subspace Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking along a descent direction obtained from a reduced subspace model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a subspace matrix \(S_k\), and a reduced direction \(s_k\) such that \(d_k=S_ks_k\) obeys \(\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), choose \(\bar\alpha_k>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(c\in(0,1)\). Select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) for which
\[
f(x_k+\beta^{j_k}\bar\alpha_kd_k)\leq f(x_k)+c\beta^{j_k}\bar\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k.
\]
Set \(\alpha_k=\beta^{j_k}\bar\alpha_k\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop according to a prescribed stationarity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a reduced descent direction, backtrack its step length until Armijo decrease holds, and update the full-space iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable near the search ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies the Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality along \(d_k=S_ks_k\).

notation.meaning: full-space direction lifted from reduced coordinates

children.title: Regularized Subspace Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Interfaces using regularization to control reduced-model steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Subspace Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization ensuring a uniquely solvable and bounded reduced first-order model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given projected gradient \(g_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\), a symmetric reduced model matrix \(B_k\), and \(\lambda_k>\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\}\), define
\[
m_k^{\mathrm{reg}}(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}(B_k+\lambda_kI)s.
\]
Compute \(s_k=-(B_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}g_k\) and propose \(x_k+S_ks_k\). Accept or reject the proposal using the method's prescribed actual-versus-predicted decrease test; after rejection, increase \(\lambda_k\). The eigenvalue condition makes the regularized model strongly convex and the reduced step unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add enough positive quadratic regularization to make the reduced model strongly convex, compute its unique step, and increase regularization after unsuccessful proposals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k+\lambda_kI\succ0\), and \(s_k=-(B_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}g_k\) uniquely minimizes \(m_k^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: shifting a symmetric matrix beyond its negative minimum eigenvalue makes it positive definite

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral shift and closed-form minimizer are correct, and the algorithm kind fits a regularized safeguard. A source is still required for the stated actual-versus-predicted acceptance mechanism and mandatory increase of the regularization parameter after rejection.

children.title: Trust-Region Subspace Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Interfaces restricting reduced-model steps to trusted regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Subspace Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-constrained reduced-model minimization with acceptance based on actual and predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), \(S_k\), a reduced model \(m_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\), compute an exact or approximate solution \(s_k\) of
\[
\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}m_k(s).
\]
When \(m_k(0)>m_k(s_k)\), form
\[
\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+S_ks_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.
\]
For a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+S_ks_k\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta\), and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Update \(\Delta_k\) by a prescribed rule that contracts it after poor agreement and may enlarge it after good boundary steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrain the reduced step by a trust-region radius, compare actual with predicted decrease, and accept or reject while adapting the radius.
assumptions_latex: The trust-region subproblem has a specified solution-accuracy rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted step satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(x_k+S_ks_k)\geq\eta\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: ratio of actual to predicted decrease

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: trust-region acceptance uses the actual-to-predicted decrease ratio

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trust-region ratio, acceptance implication, and content kind are appropriate, but the complete subspace trust-region interface and radius-update policy lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Safeguard Activation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Model-quality conditions motivating stronger subspace-step protection.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Activation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate selecting unguarded, regularized, or trust-region treatment of a reduced model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) be the reduced curvature matrix, let \(s_k^{\mathrm{raw}}\) be the unrestricted model step when defined, and fix thresholds \(\mu>0\) and \(\Delta_k>0\). The safeguard is inactive precisely when
\[
\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\geq\mu\quad\text{and}\quad\|s_k^{\mathrm{raw}}\|\leq\Delta_k.
\]
If the spectral inequality fails, activate regularization and choose \(\lambda_k\geq\mu-\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\). If only the norm inequality fails, activate the trust-region constraint \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\). If both fail, either safeguard may be used provided the resulting reduced model is bounded below and its accepted step respects the radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the raw step only when reduced curvature is sufficiently positive and its norm is safe; otherwise activate regularization, a trust region, or both.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k^{\mathrm{raw}}\) is tested only when the unrestricted model has a finite step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Safeguard activation is determined by failure of \(\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\geq\mu\) or \(\|s_k^{\mathrm{raw}}\|\leq\Delta_k\).
review_flags: activation thresholds are one coherent design convention rather than a universal canonical regime

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Projected Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic error bounds for approximate gradients and curvature after projection into a subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), let the exact projected quantities be \(g_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}H_kS_k\), where \(H_k\) is a full-space model matrix. Approximations \(\widetilde g_k\) and \(\widetilde B_k\) have admissible projected inexactness at tolerances \(\varepsilon_{g,k},\varepsilon_{B,k}\geq0\) when
\[
\|\widetilde g_k-g_k\|\leq\varepsilon_{g,k},
\qquad
\|\widetilde B_k-B_k\|_{2}\leq\varepsilon_{B,k}.
\]
A reduced model using these quantities must carry both tolerances into its step-acceptance or convergence test; zero tolerances recover exact projected information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected gradient and curvature data are admissibly inexact when their norm errors are bounded by declared tolerances that are propagated into acceptance or convergence tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde g_k\) and \(\widetilde B_k\) satisfy the declared projected-information error budget.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic oracle inexactness is expressed by norm-bounded errors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm-bounded projected errors form a coherent condition and match the leaf, but the requirement that both tolerances be carried into acceptance or convergence tests is underspecified and unsupported. A chapter-specific source is needed to determine the intended scaling and propagation rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Reduced Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative first-order residual criterion for accepting an approximate reduced-model solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, with initial reduced point \(0\), and let \(\widehat s_k\) be returned by an inner solver. For a prescribed \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\), the reduced subproblem is solved to admissible relative first-order accuracy when
\[
m_k(\widehat s_k)\leq m_k(0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|\nabla m_k(\widehat s_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|\nabla m_k(0)\|.
\]
The first inequality prevents acceptance of a nondecreasing inner iterate, while the second quantifies approximate stationarity. When \(\nabla m_k(0)=0\), admissibility requires \(\nabla m_k(\widehat s_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an approximate reduced solution only if it decreases the model and reduces the model-gradient norm by the required relative factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat s_k\) is model-decreasing and satisfies the prescribed relative reduced-stationarity tolerance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inexact smooth subproblems commonly use model-decrease and relative-gradient residual tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model-decrease and relative-gradient tests are internally precise and the condition kind is appropriate, but this particular conjunction is a method-specific admissibility criterion and has no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Lifting to Full Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-controlled error in converting a reduced step into a full-space displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), let \(s_k\in\mathbb{R}^p\) be a reduced step, and let \(d_k=S_ks_k\) be its exact lift. A computed displacement \(\widetilde d_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is an admissible approximate lift with tolerance \(\varepsilon_{L,k}\geq0\) when
\[
\|\widetilde d_k-S_ks_k\|\leq\varepsilon_{L,k}\|S_ks_k\|.
\]
With the convention that a zero exact lift requires \(\widetilde d_k=0\), the next trial point is \(x_k^{+}=x_k+\widetilde d_k\). Consequently,
\[
\|x_k^{+}-(x_k+S_ks_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_{L,k}\|S_ks_k\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate lift is acceptable when its full-space displacement differs from the exact lifted reduced step by at most a declared relative norm error.
assumptions_latex: The same norm is used on both full-space error terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximate trial point lies within relative error \(\varepsilon_{L,k}\) of the exactly lifted trial point.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: relative forward error gives a directly verifiable lifting criterion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative forward-error condition and its trial-point consequence are mathematically consistent, and the condition kind fits. The selected relative lifting-error model is method-specific and lacks a supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Random Pursuit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-direction method using exact or approximate minimization on a sampled affine line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample a nonzero direction \(u_k\) from a specified distribution, choose a directional-search tolerance \(\delta_k\geq0\), and return \(\alpha_k\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_ku_k)\leq\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}f(x_k+\alpha u_k)+\delta_k.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ku_k\). Stop when a prescribed iteration, evaluation, or stationarity budget is reached, and output the best evaluated iterate. The case \(\delta_k=0\) is exact directional search; positive \(\delta_k\) specifies additive search error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample one nonzero direction, approximately minimize the objective along its affine line, update by the resulting scalar step, and retain the best evaluated iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below on each sampled search line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) achieves directional objective error at most \(\delta_k\) relative to the best point on \(x_k+\operatorname{span}\{u_k\}\).

source_refs.source_title: Practical Optimization: Algorithms and Engineering Applications

review_flags: locator supports one-dimensional search but not the random-direction sampling framework

source_witnesses.source_title: Practical Optimization: Algorithms and Engineering Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited chapter supports one-dimensional optimization but not random-direction pursuit. In addition, boundedness below on a sampled line does not guarantee attainment when \(\delta_k=0\); the exact case requires a nonempty line-search argmin or an explicit failure branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Multidirectional Random Pursuit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random pursuit over a sampled multidimensional subspace with an additive reduced-search tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) with \(p\geq2\), choose \(\delta_k\geq0\), and compute \(s_k\in\mathbb{R}^p\) such that
\[
f(x_k+S_ks_k)\leq\inf_{s\in\mathbb{R}^p}f(x_k+S_ks)+\delta_k.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+S_ks_k\). Stop at a prescribed iteration, evaluation, or stationarity budget and output the best evaluated iterate. Rank-deficient samples are permitted only if the intended search space is \(\operatorname{range}(S_k)\); otherwise require \(S_k\) to have full column rank almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample several directions, approximately minimize over their joint span, lift the reduced minimizer, and output the best point found within the prescribed budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) has objective error at most \(\delta_k\) relative to the minimum over the sampled affine subspace.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multidirectional pursuit replaces scalar line search by optimization over a sampled affine subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and multidirectional subspace formulation fit the leaf, but no source supports this random-subspace pursuit interface. Moreover, boundedness below on the sampled affine subspace does not guarantee existence of a returned minimizer when \(\delta_k=0\).

children.title: Exact Directional Search
children.top_down_role: Directional-search variants targeting exact minimization along sampled directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Directional Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global minimization of the objective along the complete affine line generated by a direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and a nonzero direction \(u_k\), define the univariate restriction \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha u_k)\). Compute any
\[
\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}\phi_k(\alpha),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ku_k\). If the argmin is not unique, apply a declared deterministic tie-breaking rule; if it is empty, the exact-search interface reports failure. When \(f\) is differentiable and \(\alpha_k\) is an interior minimizer, exact search implies \(u_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_{k+1})=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally minimize the objective along the entire affine line, update with a selected minimizer, and report failure if no line minimizer exists.
assumptions_latex: For directional orthogonality, \(f\) is differentiable at \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k+\alpha u_k)\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\); differentiability gives \(u_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_{k+1})=0\).

notation.meaning: objective restricted to the sampled affine line

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Directional Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive- or relative-accuracy line search along one sampled direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\). For a nonempty search set \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) with \(\inf_{\alpha\in I}f(x+\alpha u)>-\infty\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), a scalar \(\widehat\alpha\in I\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-inexact directional-search solution when
\[
f(x+\widehat\alpha u)\le \inf_{\alpha\in I}f(x+\alpha u)+\varepsilon.
\]
The associated directional-pursuit update is \(x^+=x+\widehat\alpha u\). If additionally \(0\in I\), a relative-accuracy variant with prescribed \(\rho\in(0,1]\) requires
\[
f(x)-f(x+\widehat\alpha u)\ge \rho\left(f(x)-\inf_{\alpha\in I}f(x+\alpha u)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact directional search returns a feasible step whose objective is within an additive tolerance of the best value along the search set. When the zero step is feasible, relative accuracy can instead require a prescribed fraction of the best attainable decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=x+\widehat\alpha u\) satisfies the selected directional-search accuracy criterion.

children.title: Search-Accuracy Effects
children.top_down_role: Impact of directional-search accuracy on progress, robustness, and work.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Accuracy Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive search error weakens one-step directional descent by the same amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and, for a unit vector \(u\), the function \(\alpha\mapsto f(x+\alpha u)\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz derivative. If an unrestricted inexact search returns \(\widehat\alpha\) satisfying \(f(x+\widehat\alpha u)\le\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}f(x+\alpha u)+\varepsilon\), then
\[
f(x+\widehat\alpha u)\le f(x)-\frac{\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle^2}{2L}+\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently, strict certified decrease is guaranteed whenever \(\varepsilon<\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle^2/(2L)\); errors comparable to or larger than this directional decrease can erase the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive line-search error subtracts directly from the ideal directional decrease; descent remains certified only when the error is smaller than that decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x+\widehat\alpha u)-f(x)\le-\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle^2/(2L)+\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Sketch Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One random subspace sketch and one projected-gradient update per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample a full-column-rank sketch \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\), form the orthogonal projector
\[
P_k=S_k(S_k^{\mathsf T}S_k)^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T},
\]
and choose \(\eta_k>0\). Perform the single-sketch update
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(x_k).
\]
Stop when a prescribed budget or stationarity test is met, and output the latest iterate. The method uses one sampled subspace and one gradient projection at each iteration; \(q=1\) gives a random-direction gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration samples one subspace, projects the current gradient onto it, and takes a step using only that projected component.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) has full column rank almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(x_k)\) is the next single-sketch iterate.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the sampled subspace

children.title: Block Subspace-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods using structured groups of subspace-gradient components.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Subspace-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient updates restricted to one block from a fixed subspace decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\) have orthonormal columns and satisfy \(\sum_{j=1}^mU_jU_j^{\mathsf T}=I_n\). Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), select a block index \(J_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), compute the block gradient \(g_k=U_{J_k}^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\), and update
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_{k,J_k}U_{J_k}g_k.
\]
The index may be cycled or sampled with positive probabilities. Stop under a prescribed budget or stationarity rule and return the latest iterate. Only coordinates in \(\operatorname{range}(U_{J_k})\) change during iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block method selects one subspace from a fixed decomposition and changes only the gradient coordinates belonging to that block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}-x_k\in\operatorname{range}(U_{J_k})\) and equals \(-\eta_{k,J_k}U_{J_k}U_{J_k}^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\).

children.title: Minibatch Subspace-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods aggregating multiple randomized subspace-gradient samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Minibatch Subspace-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent sketched-gradient estimates are averaged before each update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and batch size \(b\ge1\), iteration \(k\) independently samples sketches \(S_{k,1},\ldots,S_{k,b}\). From each sketch construct a subspace-gradient estimator \(G(x_k;S_{k,i})\in\mathbb{R}^n\), form
\[
\overline G_k=\frac1b\sum_{i=1}^bG(x_k;S_{k,i}),
\qquad
x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_k\overline G_k,
\]
with \(\eta_k>0\). Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity test and output the latest iterate. When the component estimators are conditionally unbiased, their average is conditionally unbiased and its conditional covariance is divided by \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minibatch method averages several independent sketched-gradient estimates, reducing estimator variance before taking the gradient step.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x_k\), the sketches \(S_{k,i}\) are independent and identically distributed.
\(\mathbb{E}[G(x_k;S_{k,i})\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\) when unbiasedness is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_k\overline G_k\), with \(\operatorname{Cov}(\overline G_k\mid x_k)=\operatorname{Cov}(G(x_k;S_{k,1})\mid x_k)/b\).

notation.meaning: number of sketches in the minibatch

children.title: Batch-Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Progress, variance, and resource tradeoffs across aggregation sizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance benefit and oracle cost as functions of minibatch size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_b\) be conditionally independent estimators satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[G_i\mid x]=\nabla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|G_i-\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\mid x]\le\sigma^2\). Then \(\overline G_b=b^{-1}\sum_iG_i\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb{E}[\|\overline G_b-\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\mid x]\le\frac{\sigma^2}{b}.
\]
Thus \(b=1\) is the single-sample regime, \(1<b<B\) is the variance-reduction regime, and \(b\ge B\) is a saturation regime whenever only \(B\) independent samples or parallel workers are available. Serial oracle cost is \(b\) estimator calls per update, so variance decreases linearly in \(1/b\) while serial work grows linearly in \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing batch size divides independent estimator variance by the batch size but multiplies serial oracle work; benefits saturate at the independence or parallelism limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\|\overline G_b-\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\mid x]\le\sigma^2/b\), at a serial cost of \(b\) estimator calls.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variance bound and serial estimator-count statement are correct, but the cited locator does not support them. Moreover, the proposed threshold B conflates a finite supply of independent samples with a parallel-worker limit: exceeding the worker count need not stop statistical variance reduction, although it can limit parallel speedup. A direct source and a precise resource model are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Subspace-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric scaling inside each sampled subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), sample a full-column-rank \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\), choose a symmetric positive-definite metric \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and solve the reduced system
\[
(S_k^{\mathsf T}H_kS_k)d_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k).
\]
For \(\eta_k>0\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_kS_kd_k\). Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity criterion. Equivalently, the step applies the subspace preconditioner \(S_k(S_k^{\mathsf T}H_kS_k)^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T}\) to the full gradient without forming a full-space inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method solves a small metric-weighted system inside each sampled subspace and uses the lifted solution as a preconditioned gradient step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_kS_k(S_k^{\mathsf T}H_kS_k)^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov-Type Subspace Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extrapolated iteration followed by a randomly projected gradient correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_{-1}=x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For iteration \(k\ge0\), choose \(\beta_k\in[0,1)\), form the extrapolated point
\[
y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1}),
\]
sample a full-column-rank sketch \(S_k\), and set \(P_k=S_k(S_k^{\mathsf T}S_k)^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T}\). With \(\eta_k>0\), update
\[
x_{k+1}=y_k-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(y_k).
\]
Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity criterion and return the latest accepted iterate. A Nesterov schedule may generate \(\beta_k\) from \(t_{k+1}=(1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2})/2\) and \(\beta_k=(t_k-1)/t_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesterov-type subspace acceleration extrapolates from two iterates, then corrects the extrapolated point using a gradient projected onto a fresh random subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) has full column rank almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(y_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Momentum Subspace Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heavy-ball memory combined with a sampled subspace-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_{-1}=x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample a full-column-rank sketch \(S_k\), define \(P_k=S_k(S_k^{\mathsf T}S_k)^{-1}S_k^{\mathsf T}\), and choose \(\eta_k>0\) and \(\beta_k\in[0,1)\). The momentum subspace update is
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(x_k)+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1}).
\]
Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity test and output the latest accepted iterate. Unlike extrapolated-gradient acceleration, the gradient is evaluated at \(x_k\), while the previous displacement is added directly to the new projected-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A momentum subspace method adds the previous displacement to a gradient step projected onto the current sampled subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) has full column rank almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}-x_k=-\eta_kP_k\nabla f(x_k)+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\).

children.title: Restart Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for resetting accelerated subspace states.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-reset rule for accelerated subspace iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an accelerated subspace method maintain an accepted iterate \(x_k\), a previous iterate \(x_{k-1}\), and acceleration state \(t_k\). After evaluating a Boolean restart test \(R_k\), set
\[
(x_{k-1},t_k,\beta_k)\leftarrow(x_k,1,0)
\]
whenever \(R_k\) is true; otherwise retain the scheduled acceleration state. The next trial point is then \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\), followed by the method's sampled-subspace correction. The interface outputs the updated state and trial point. Resetting makes \(y_k=x_k\), so the first post-restart correction is an unaccelerated subspace step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a restart test fires, the interface erases momentum and resets the acceleration clock, making the next trial an ordinary subspace-gradient step.
assumptions_latex: \(R_k\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\) is computable from available iteration data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k=\mathrm{true}\) implies \(x_{k-1}=x_k\), \(t_k=1\), \(\beta_k=0\), and hence \(y_k=x_k\).

children.title: Safeguard Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for limiting or rejecting unreliable accelerated behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance filter comparing accelerated and conservative subspace candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iterate \(x_k\), let \(z_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\) be an accelerated subspace candidate and \(z_k^{\mathrm{safe}}\) a conservative candidate. Given \(c\ge0\), accept
\[
x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}
z_k^{\mathrm{acc}},&f(z_k^{\mathrm{acc}})\le f(x_k)-c\|z_k^{\mathrm{acc}}-x_k\|_2^2,\\
z_k^{\mathrm{safe}},&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
On rejection, reset the acceleration state before the next iteration. The interface requires the safe candidate to satisfy \(f(z_k^{\mathrm{safe}})\le f(x_k)\). Therefore every accepted output is nonincreasing in objective, and an accepted accelerated candidate satisfies the specified quantitative descent test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safeguard accepts an accelerated candidate only after a descent test; otherwise it uses a nonincreasing conservative step and resets acceleration.
assumptions_latex: Both candidates and their objective values are available to the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)\), and accelerated acceptance implies \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-c\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|_2^2\).

children.title: Acceleration-Failure Triggers
children.top_down_role: Observable regimes motivating restart or safeguard intervention.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration-Failure Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable conditions that request restart or safeguarded fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an accelerated trial \(z_k\) generated from \(x_k\), previous displacement \(s_k=x_k-x_{k-1}\), and proposed correction \(d_k=z_k-x_k\), define the failure trigger
\[
R_k=\bigl[f(z_k)>f(x_k)+\delta_k\bigr]\ \lor\ \bigl[\langle s_k,d_k\rangle<0\bigr]\ \lor\ \bigl[\|d_k\|_2>\Gamma_k\max\{1,\|s_k\|_2\}\bigr],
\]
where \(\delta_k\ge0\) and \(\Gamma_k>0\). The three clauses detect excessive objective growth, opposition between momentum and the proposed displacement, and anomalous step growth. If \(R_k\) is true, the recovery interface rejects or restarts the accelerated state; otherwise this trigger permits normal acceptance testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration failure is flagged by excessive objective growth, momentum opposition, or anomalous step enlargement, causing restart or safeguarded fallback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k=\mathrm{true}\) requests rejection, restart, or fallback before the accelerated state is reused.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate knowledge kind, and the formula is syntactically well-defined. However, the particular disjunction of objective growth, negative displacement alignment, and normalized step growth is a designed interface rule rather than a universal acceleration-failure criterion. No source is supplied for this exact trigger or its interpretation.

children.title: Projection Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The geometric view based on projection in a selected metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted projection form of one sketch-and-project step for a consistent linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\operatorname{Range}(A)\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, and \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\). One sketch-and-project step is
\[
x^{+}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_B^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Writing \(M_S=S^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S\), its unique solution is
\[
x^{+}=x^k-B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S M_S^{\dagger}S^{\mathsf T}(Ax^k-b).
\]
Thus the iteration projects the current point, in the \(B\)-metric, onto the solution set of the sampled equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next iterate is the weighted Euclidean projection of the current iterate onto the affine set defined by the sampled linear equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{+}=\Pi^{B}_{\{x:S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b\}}(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Squared norm induced by the positive-definite matrix B.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard weighted projection solution obtained from the KKT system

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted projection representation and pseudoinverse formula are mathematically precise and fit the terminal container, but no inspectable citation supports the sketch-and-project specialization.

children.title: Affine-Intersection Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The geometric view based on sampled affine solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Intersection Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric interpretation of a sampled linear constraint as an affine intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), define the sampled affine set
\[
\mathcal L_S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b\}.
\]
If \(Ax=b\) is consistent, then its solution set \(\mathcal L=\{x:Ax=b\}\) satisfies \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal L_S\), and
\[
\mathcal L_S=x_\star+\operatorname{Null}(S^{\mathsf T}A)
\]
for every \(x_\star\in\mathcal L\). For sketches \(S_1,\ldots,S_r\), the accumulated sampled constraints satisfy
\[
\bigcap_{j=1}^r\mathcal L_{S_j}=\{x:S_j^{\mathsf T}Ax=S_j^{\mathsf T}b\text{ for all }j\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each sketch defines an affine superset of the exact solution set; intersecting sampled sets accumulates the corresponding sampled equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal L_S=x_\star+\operatorname{Null}(S^{\mathsf T}A)\).

notation.meaning: Exact affine solution set of the linear system.
Affine solution set of the sketched equations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary affine geometry of consistent linear equations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-set identities are correct under the stated consistency assumption and the representation kind fits the container, but the record has no source reference with a specific locator.

children.title: Inconsistent-Intersection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interpretive boundaries arising when sampled affine sets are incompatible.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent-Intersection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the literal projection interpretation when a sampled affine constraint is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For arbitrary \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and sketch \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), the sampled affine set \(\mathcal L_S=\{x:S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b\}\) is nonempty exactly when
\[
S^{\mathsf T}b\in\operatorname{Range}(S^{\mathsf T}A),
\]
equivalently,
\[
\bigl(I-S^{\mathsf T}A(S^{\mathsf T}A)^\dagger\bigr)S^{\mathsf T}b=0.
\]
If this condition fails, the constrained projection onto \(\mathcal L_S\) is undefined. A pseudoinverse residual update then represents a least-squares correction to the sampled equations, not a projection onto their empty exact intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled constraint is projectable exactly when its right-hand side lies in the sampled operator’s range; otherwise pseudoinverse updates have only a least-squares interpretation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_S=\varnothing\iff S^{\mathsf T}b\notin\operatorname{Range}(S^{\mathsf T}A)\).

notation.meaning: Exact solution set of the sampled equations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solvability criterion for a finite-dimensional linear equation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sampled-system solvability criterion is standard and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate. A source is still required for the stronger method-specific assertion that the pseudoinverse update in the inconsistent regime should be interpreted as a least-squares correction.

children.title: Random-Solve Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The view centered on solving a randomly sketched reduced system.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Solve Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small random linear solve induced by a freshly sampled sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^k\), sample \(S_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\) and form
\[
M_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k,
\qquad r_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k).
\]
Compute the minimum-norm solution
\[
y^k=M_k^\dagger r_k
\]
of the sampled system; when the system is consistent, this satisfies \(M_k y^k=r_k\). Return the pair \((S_k,y^k)\) to the update stage. The expensive ambient system is therefore replaced at each iteration by a random system of dimension \(q\), followed by multiplication with \(B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration samples a sketch and solves the resulting small Gram system for coefficients that determine the ambient-space correction.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) is sampled from a prescribed distribution independently of future sketches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k=(S_k^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k)^\dagger S_k^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum-norm coefficients from the random solve.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic decomposition of the sketch-and-project formula
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The random Gram solve is well specified and algorithm is the correct content kind, but no cited source supports this decomposition as the intended random-solve interpretation.

children.title: Random-Update Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The view centered on applying a randomized correction in the original space.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Update Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient update generated from the coefficients of the sampled solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(S_k\), obtain coefficients \(y^k\) from the sketched solve, and set
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k y^k.
\]
Equivalently, with \(M_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k\),
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_kM_k^\dagger S_k^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k).
\]
After a prescribed number \(K\) of iterations or satisfaction of a chosen residual test, output \(x^K\). The correction always lies in the random subspace \(\operatorname{Range}(B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The small random-solve coefficients are lifted through the sketched adjoint to produce a correction lying in a random primal subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}-x^k\in\operatorname{Range}(B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k)\).

children.title: Primal-Update Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between reduced solves and full-space corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Update Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between the random-solve lift and the weighted primal projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(Ax=b\) is consistent and \(B\succ0\). For a fixed sketch \(S_k\), let
\[
y^k=(S_k^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k)^\dagger S_k^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k).
\]
Then the lifted update
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k y^k
\]
is exactly the unique solution of
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_B^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad S_k^{\mathsf T}Ax=S_k^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Hence the random-solve and primal projection descriptions define the same iterate, including when the sketched Gram matrix is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the small sketched system and lifting its coefficients produces exactly the weighted projection onto the sampled affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S_k y^k=\Pi^B_{\{x:S_k^{\mathsf T}Ax=S_k^{\mathsf T}b\}}(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum-norm solution of the sketched Gram system.

children.title: Fixed-Point Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The view of randomized projection as a stochastic fixed-point process.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sketch-and-project step viewed as a random fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each sketch \(S\), define
\[
T_S(x)=x-B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S(S^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S)^\dagger S^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b).
\]
If \(B\succ0\), then
\[
\operatorname{Fix}(T_S)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b\}.
\]
Consequently, the randomized iteration \(x^{k+1}=T_{S_k}(x^k)\) is a random fixed-point iteration. Its almost-sure common fixed-point set is
\[
\mathcal F=\{x:T_S(x)=x\text{ for almost every }S\},
\]
which equals the exact solution set when the sketch distribution is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sampled projection is a fixed-point map whose fixed points solve that sketch; an exact sketch distribution makes their common fixed points solve the full system.
assumptions_latex: The sampled affine equation is consistent almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=T_{S_k}(x^k)\) and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T_S)=\{x:S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b\}\).

notation.meaning: Fixed-point operator associated with sketch S.
Set of fixed points of the sampled operator.

children.title: Dual Interpretation
children.top_down_role: The view expressed through dual variables or dual optimization geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concave quadratic dual of the sampled weighted projection problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\), and let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Consider the feasible sampled projection problem
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_B^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad S^{\mathsf T}Ax=S^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Its Lagrange dual is
\[
\operatorname*{maximize}_{y\in\mathbb R^q}\ d_S(y),
\qquad d_S(y)=y^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k)-\frac12y^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}Sy.
\]
Strong duality holds. One dual maximizer is
\[
y^\star=(S^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S)^\dagger S^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k),
\]
and its associated primal optimizer is \(x^\star=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}Sy^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible sampled projection problem has a concave quadratic dual, and a pseudoinverse dual maximizer supplies coefficients whose affine lift is the unique primal projection.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac12\lVert x^\star-x^k\rVert_B^2=d_S(y^\star)\) and \(x^\star=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}Sy^\star\).

notation.meaning: Concave quadratic dual objective for sketch S.
Multiplier for the sampled equality constraint.

children.title: Primal-Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between primal projections and dual representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine map carrying dual sketch coefficients to the unique primal projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y^\star\) maximize the sampled dual quadratic and define
\[
x^\star=x^k+B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}Sy^\star.
\]
Then the pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) satisfies
\[
B(x^\star-x^k)-A^{\mathsf T}Sy^\star=0,
\qquad S^{\mathsf T}Ax^\star=S^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Conversely, any pair satisfying these two equations is primal-dual optimal. The primal optimizer \(x^\star\) is unique because \(B\succ0\), although \(y^\star\) need not be unique when \(S^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}S\) is singular; all dual maximizers induce the same primal correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual solutions correspond through an affine lift; dual coefficients may be nonunique, but every dual maximizer yields the same unique projected point.
assumptions_latex: The sampled affine constraint is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is optimal if and only if \(B(x^\star-x^k)=A^{\mathsf T}Sy^\star\) and \(S^{\mathsf T}Ax^\star=S^{\mathsf T}b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: KKT characterization of an equality-constrained strongly convex quadratic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Kaczmarz Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical randomized row-projection method for a consistent linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the nonzero rows of \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\), and suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with probabilities \(p_i>0\) and update
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\frac{b_{i_k}-a_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}x^k}{\lVert a_{i_k}\rVert_2^2}a_{i_k}.
\]
After \(K\) iterations or satisfaction of a residual stopping rule, output \(x^K\). The standard norm-proportional specialization uses \(p_i=\lVert a_i\rVert_2^2/\lVert A\rVert_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized Kaczmarz samples a row and orthogonally projects the current iterate onto that row equation, commonly using probabilities proportional to squared row norms.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical randomized Kaczmarz row-projection update
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The row-projection update and norm-proportional specialization correctly describe the randomized Kaczmarz family, and algorithm is the appropriate kind. The record nevertheless supplies no citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kaczmarz iteration for a consistent normalized linear system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the row-projection update, its stochastic-gradient interpretation when indices are sampled, and its error propagation for normalized consistent linear equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\|a_i\|=1\) for \(i=1,\ldots,N\), and suppose that there exists \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(a_i^Tx^*=b_i\) for every \(i\). For \(f(x)=\frac{1}{2N}\sum_{i=1}^N(a_i^Tx-b_i)^2\), the component-gradient update with unit stepsize and index \(i_k\) is \[x^{k+1}=x^k-a_{i_k}(a_{i_k}^Tx^k-b_{i_k})=x^k-a_{i_k}a_{i_k}^T(x^k-x^*).\] When the indices are selected randomly, this is the randomized Kaczmarz method. Each update is the orthogonal projection of \(x^k\) onto \(\{x:a_{i_k}^Tx=b_{i_k}\}\), and \[x^{k+1}-x^*=\left(\prod_{j=0}^{k}(I-a_{i_j}a_{i_j}^T)\right)(x^0-x^*),\] with the factors ordered according to the iteration sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For unit-norm rows of a consistent linear system, a unit-stepsize component-gradient update on the finite-sum least-squares objective is a Kaczmarz row projection. Random index selection gives the randomized Kaczmarz method. The error after successive updates is the ordered product of the corresponding orthogonal-complement projectors applied to the initial error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=x^k-a_{i_k}(a_{i_k}^Tx^k-b_{i_k})=\operatorname{proj}_{\{x:a_{i_k}^Tx=b_{i_k}\}}(x^k),\quad x^{k+1}-x^*=\left(\prod_{j=0}^{k}(I-a_{i_j}a_{i_j}^T)\right)(x^0-x^*)

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Gauss–Seidel Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized exact coordinate minimization for linear least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2\), write the nonzero columns of \(A\) as \(A_{:j}\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(j_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with probabilities \(p_j>0\) and set
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\frac{A_{:j_k}^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k)}{\lVert A_{:j_k}\rVert_2^2}e_{j_k}.
\]
This update exactly minimizes \(f(x^k+te_{j_k})\) over \(t\in\mathbb R\). After \(K\) iterations or a stopping test, output \(x^K\). A standard choice is \(p_j=\lVert A_{:j}\rVert_2^2/\lVert A\rVert_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized Gauss–Seidel samples a coordinate and exactly minimizes the least-squares objective along that coordinate, often with column-norm-proportional sampling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in x^k+\operatorname{span}\{e_{j_k}\}}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian-Pursuit Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian one-dimensional sketch-and-project update for linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Ax=b\) be consistent and \(B\succ0\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(s_k\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\) in \(\mathbb R^m\), set \(d_k=B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}s_k\), and, when \(d_k\neq0\), update
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\frac{s_k^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k)}{s_k^{\mathsf T}AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}s_k}d_k.
\]
If \(d_k=0\), leave the iterate unchanged or resample. After \(K\) iterations or a stopping test, output \(x^K\). This is the rank-one sketch-and-project method with Gaussian sketch \(S_k=s_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian sketch generates a random pursuit direction through the adjoint; an exact line coefficient projects the iterate onto the sampled scalar equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k^{\mathsf T}Ax^{k+1}=s_k^{\mathsf T}b\) whenever \(B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}s_k\neq0\).

notation.meaning: Covariance matrix of the Gaussian sketch.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Block Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines block-selection matrices whose sampled subspaces respect a fixed coordinate partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A structured block sketch is a random matrix \(S_I\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_I}\), indexed by a random set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), whose columns are the coordinate vectors \(e_j\) with \(j\in\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i\). Its range is therefore \(\operatorname{range}(S_I)=\{h\in\mathbb{R}^n:h_j=0\text{ for }j\notin\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i\}\). The associated orthogonal sketch projector is \(P_I=S_I(S_I^{\mathsf T}S_I)^{-1}S_I^{\mathsf T}\); for coordinate-selection sketches, \(S_I^{\mathsf T}S_I\) is the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured block sketch selects whole blocks from a fixed coordinate partition and projects vectors onto the coordinates contained in those blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(S_I)\) is precisely the coordinate subspace supported on the sampled blocks.
