knowledge_statements.title: Block-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies coordinate block sketches by sampled dimension per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the blocks sampled at iteration \(k\), and define the sampled dimension by \(q_k=\sum_{i\in I_k}|B_i|\). The singleton regime has \(q_k=1\); a fixed-block regime has \(q_k=q\) for a prescribed \(1<q<n\); a variable-block regime allows \(q_k\) to vary; and the full-space regime has \(q_k=n\). A bounded-size regime satisfies deterministic bounds \(1\le q_{\min}\le q_k\le q_{\max}\le n\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-size regimes distinguish singleton, fixed, variable, bounded, and full-space sketches according to the number of coordinates updated per iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\) is the sampled set of blocks at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k=\sum_{i\in I_k}|B_i|\) determines the block-size regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Block Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines block sketches generated by a coordinate cover rather than a partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be nonempty coordinate blocks satisfying \(\bigcup_{i=1}^mB_i=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), without requiring pairwise disjointness. An overlapping block sketch samples \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and uses the coordinate subspace supported on \(U_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i\). Its selection matrix \(S_I\) contains each coordinate vector \(e_j\), \(j\in U_I\), once. The overlap multiplicity is \(\omega=max_{1\le j\le n}|\{i:j\in B_i\}|\); the sketch is genuinely overlapping exactly when \(\omega>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping block sketches sample from a covering of coordinates in which one coordinate may belong to several blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sampled subspace is supported on \(U_I\), and \(\omega>1\) characterizes overlap.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Sketch Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes history-dependent sketch sampling while preserving conditional coverage of every direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all randomness and iterates observed before iteration \(k\), and let \(P_k\) be the orthogonal projector associated with the selected sketch. The selection rule is adaptive and uniformly covering if its conditional distribution is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and there exists \(\rho>0\) such that \[\mathbb E[P_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\succeq \rho I\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.\] Equivalently, every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\|P_kv\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\ge\rho\|v\|^2\). Thus past information may change the sampling probabilities, but no direction can lose all conditional probability of being explored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive selection may depend on the observed history, provided its conditional expected projector continues to cover every direction uniformly.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\)'s conditional law may depend on \(\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[P_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\succeq\rho I\) guarantees uniform conditional directional coverage.

notation.meaning: information available before sketch k is drawn

review_flags: no supplied locator supports this adaptive conditional-coverage formulation
exact exploration condition may vary by convergence theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional positive-definiteness condition is mathematically coherent and the projector identity is valid, but it is one particular uniform-exploration assumption rather than a source-independent definition of adaptive selection. No citation establishes that this exact condition is canonical for the target method family.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Sketch Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregates simultaneously computed sketched directions with a controlled relaxation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), draw \(r\) sketches \(S_{k,1},\ldots,S_{k,r}\). In parallel, worker \(j\) computes a direction \(d_{k,j}\in\operatorname{range}(S_{k,j})\) from the common point \(x_k\). Choose weights \(w_{k,j}\ge0\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^r w_{k,j}=1\), a relaxation \(\alpha_k>0\), and update \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k\sum_{j=1}^r w_{k,j}d_{k,j}.\] Stop when a prescribed residual or objective-decrease test is met; otherwise return the last iterate. For constrained problems, the aggregation is admissible only when the displayed update remains in the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute sketched directions from one iterate in parallel, then combine them by a weighted, relaxed update subject to feasibility.
assumptions_latex: All workers use the same base iterate \(x_k\).
Each \(d_{k,j}\) belongs to its worker's sampled subspace.
The weights form a convex combination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k\sum_{j=1}^r w_{k,j}d_{k,j}\).

notation.meaning: sketch used by worker j at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Subspace Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a Euclidean proximal-gradient update restricted to a randomly sampled linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), initialize \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}g\). At iteration \(k\), sample a full-column-rank matrix \(S_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times q_k}\), choose \(\eta_k>0\), and compute \[u_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb R^{q_k}}\left\{\langle S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k),u\rangle+g(x_k+S_ku)+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|S_ku\|^2\right\}.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+S_ku_k\). Stop when a prescribed stationarity test holds, and return the last iterate. The update changes only components contained in \(\operatorname{range}(S_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration minimizes a proximal-gradient model only along a randomly sampled subspace and adds the resulting restricted step to the iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
The displayed subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}-x_k\in\operatorname{range}(S_k)\) and minimizes the restricted proximal-gradient model.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Forward–Backward Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States forward–backward splitting performed on the affine subspace selected at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To solve \(0\in A(x)+B(x)\) in \(\mathbb R^n\), initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), choose an orthogonal projector \(P_k\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), then select \(x_{k+1}\in x_k+\operatorname{range}(P_k)\) satisfying \[0\in P_kB(x_k)+P_kA(x_{k+1})+\frac{1}{\gamma_k}(x_{k+1}-x_k).\] Equivalently, in coordinates \(S_k\) spanning the subspace, solve the corresponding restricted resolvent inclusion. Stop when a prescribed residual vanishes within tolerance; return the last iterate. With \(A=\partial g\) and \(B=\nabla f\), this is subspace proximal gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward evaluation and backward resolvent step are restricted to the sampled affine subspace; proximal gradient is the subdifferential-gradient specialization.
assumptions_latex: The restricted inclusion admits a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The new iterate satisfies the projected forward–backward inclusion on \(x_k+\operatorname{range}(P_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subspace Proximal Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an implementable residual criterion for an approximate restricted proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the restricted proximal-gradient model \[Q_k(u)=\langle S_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k),u\rangle+g(x_k+S_ku)+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|S_ku\|^2,\] a computed vector \(\widetilde u_k\) is residually \(\varepsilon_k\)-inexact if there exist \(v_k\in\partial g(x_k+S_k\widetilde u_k)\) and \(r_k\in\mathbb R^{q_k}\) such that \[r_k=S_k^{\mathsf T}(\nabla f(x_k)+v_k)+\frac{1}{\eta_k}S_k^{\mathsf T}S_k\widetilde u_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\le\varepsilon_k.\] The inexact update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+S_k\widetilde u_k\); exact solution corresponds to \(\varepsilon_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate subspace proximal step is accepted when a computable first-order residual for its restricted model is at most the specified tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_k\|\le\varepsilon_k\) quantifies first-order inexactness of the restricted proximal subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Block Conditional-Gradient Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a projection-free update using a linear minimization oracle on a randomly selected feasible block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. Initialize \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), call the block linear oracle \[s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s
i C_{i_k}}\langle\nabla_{i_k}f(x_k),s\rangle,\] choose \(\gamma_k\in[0,1]\), and set \((x_{k+1})_{i_k}=(1-\gamma_k)(x_k)_{i_k}+\gamma_ks_k\), leaving all other blocks unchanged. Stop when a prescribed block or global Frank–Wolfe gap is within tolerance; return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method samples one feasible block, solves its linear minimization problem, and takes a convex-combination step without projecting onto the full feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Every block linear oracle attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in C\) and only block \(i_k\) changes.

canonical sampling and gap conventions require source confirmation

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Atom Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines linear atom minimization over the atoms exposed by a selected sketch or block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\subset\mathbb R^n\), where \(\mathcal A\) is an atom set, and let a sketch \(S
i\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) determine a nonempty eligible subset \(\mathcal A(S,x)subseteq\mathcal A\) at the current point \(x\). For a linearization vector \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), restricted atom search returns \[a_S
i\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathcal A(S,x)}\langle g,a\rangle.\] A common block restriction takes \(\mathcal A(S,x)\) to be atoms whose feasible displacement \(a-x\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(S)\). The restricted gap is \(G_S(x;g)=\langle g,x-a_S\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted atom search minimizes the current linear model only over atoms eligible under the sampled sketch, producing a sketch-local conditional-gradient gap.
assumptions_latex: The restricted linear minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_S\) minimizes the linearization over eligible atoms and defines \(G_S(x;g)\).

notation.meaning: atoms eligible under sketch S at x

review_flags: no supplied locator supports sketch-restricted atom sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended definition is plausible, but no citation supports the application-dependent eligible-atom construction. The statement also contains multiple malformed relations: \(S\ni\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), an unescaped `subseteq`, and \(a_S\ni\operatorname*{argmin}\). Because the exact eligibility convention is source-sensitive, a sourced correction is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Sketch-Aware Linear Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines additive and multiplicative accuracy for a linear oracle restricted by the current sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x\in C\), a sketch-dependent feasible set \(D_S(x)\subseteq C\), and \(g
i\mathbb R^n\), define the restricted gap optimum by \(G_S^*(x;g)=\max_{z\in D_S(x)}\langle g,x-z\rangle\). An output \(\widetilde s_S\in D_S(x)\) is an additive \(\varepsilon\)-oracle if \[\langle g,x-widetilde s_S\rangle\ge G_S^*(x;g)-\varepsilon.\] It is a multiplicative \(\delta\)-oracle if \[\langle g,x-widetilde s_S\rangle\ge\delta G_S^*(x;g),\qquad 0<\delta\le1.\] These conditions compare the returned atom only with the best point allowed by the same sketch, not with the unrestricted linear oracle over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch-aware approximate oracle achieves additive or multiplicative accuracy relative to the best linear improvement available inside the same sampled restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy or multiplicative \(\delta\)-accuracy relative to the restricted oracle.

notation.meaning: feasible points exposed by sketch S

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Convex Subspace Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected sublinear convergence for randomized coordinate-subspace descent under blockwise smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable, with block gradients satisfying \(\|
abla_i f(x+U_ih)-
abla_i f(x)\|\le L_i\|h\|\). Sample block \(i_k\) independently with probability \(p_i>0\) and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-U_{i_k}
abla_{i_k}f(x_k)/L_{i_k}\). If a minimizer \(x^*\) exists and the initial sublevel set has finite radius \(R\) in the norm \(\|z\|_{LP^{-1}}^2=sum_i(L_i/p_i)\|z_i\|^2\), then there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that \[\mathbb E[f(x_k)-f(x^*)]\le rac{cR^2}{k+1}.\] Hence \(O(R^2/\varepsilon)\) sampled block-gradient calls suffice for expected error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized block descent on a smooth convex objective has expected objective error of order one over the iteration count under positive sampling and bounded level-set radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and has blockwise Lipschitz gradients with constants \(L_i>0\).
The initial sublevel set has finite \(LP^{-1}\)-radius \(R\) about a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(x_k)-f(x^*)]=O(R^2/k)\), requiring \(O(R^2/\varepsilon)\) block-gradient calls.

notation.meaning: embedding of block i into the full space

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Subspace Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear expected convergence for isotropic rank-s projected gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-smooth and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with minimizer \(x_\star\). At iteration \(k\), independently sample an orthogonal projector \(P_k\) satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[P_k\mid x_k]=\rho I_d\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-L^{-1}P_k\nabla f(x_k)\). Then \[\mathbb{E}[f(x_k)-f(x_\star)]\leq (1-\rho\mu/L)^k\bigl(f(x_0)-f(x_\star)\bigr).\] Consequently, an expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) is attained after \[k\geq \frac{L}{\rho\mu}\log\!\left(\frac{f(x_0)-f(x_\star)}{\varepsilon}\right).\] For a uniformly distributed rank-\(s\) projector, \(\rho=s/d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Isotropic rank-s projected gradient descent converges linearly in expectation, with iteration complexity proportional to (d/s)(L/mu) times a logarithmic accuracy factor.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(0<\mu\leq L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[f(x_k)-f(x_\star)]\leq(1-\rho\mu/L)^k(f(x_0)-f(x_\star))\).

notation.meaning: random orthogonal projector defining the sampled search subspace
unique minimizer of the strongly convex objective

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Subspace Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected sampled-subspace stationarity for smooth lower-bounded objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\)-smooth and bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\). For orthogonal projectors \(P_k\), use \(x_{k+1}=x_k-L^{-1}P_k\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(R\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), independently of the iterates. Then \[\mathbb{E}\|P_R\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq \frac{2L\bigl(f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\bigr)}{K}.\] Thus at most \(2L(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/\varepsilon^2\) iterations suffice, up to integer rounding, to produce a random iterate whose expected squared projected-gradient norm is at most \(\varepsilon^2\). This statement certifies stationarity only in the sampled subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected gradient descent reduces the expected squared sampled-subspace gradient norm at an O(1/K) rate, without asserting full-gradient stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k=P_k^\top=P_k^2\), with sampling allowed to depend on the past but not on future randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}\|P_R\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq 2L(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/K\).

notation.meaning: finite lower bound on the objective
gradient component visible in the sampled subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Stationarity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from sampled projected gradients to the ambient gradient under conditional isotropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and suppose the random orthogonal projector \(P_k\) satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[P_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\rho I_d\), where \(g_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and \(\rho>0\). Since \(P_k^2=P_k\), \[\mathbb{E}[\|P_kg_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\rho\|g_k\|^2.\] Let \(R\) be an integer-valued random index independent of the iterate-and-sketch process. Then \[\mathbb{E}\|P_Rg_R\|^2=\rho\,\mathbb{E}\|g_R\|^2.\] Hence any bound \(\mathbb{E}\|P_Rg_R\|^2\leq B_K\) transfers to \(\mathbb{E}\|g_R\|^2\leq B_K/\rho\). If \(B_K\to0\), the selected iterates are stationary in the full ambient space in mean square.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional isotropy converts a projected-gradient bound into a full-gradient bound at the price of the reciprocal capture factor 1/rho.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k\) is measurable with respect to the pre-sketch history \(\mathcal F_k\).
\(R\) is independent of the iterate-and-sketch process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}\|g_R\|^2=\rho^{-1}\mathbb{E}\|P_Rg_R\|^2\leq B_K/\rho\).

notation.meaning: history available before drawing the iteration-k sketch
full gradient at the current iterate
upper bound on the expected squared projected-gradient certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation bound obtained from a contractive conditional-error recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E_k)_{k\geq0}\) be a nonnegative integrable error process adapted to \((\mathcal F_k)\). If constants \(a\in(0,1]\) and \(b\geq0\) satisfy \[\mathbb{E}[E_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq(1-a)E_k+b\quad\text{almost surely},\] then for every \(k\geq0\), \[\mathbb{E}E_k\leq(1-a)^k\mathbb{E}E_0+\frac{b}{a}\bigl(1-(1-a)^k\bigr).\] In particular, \(b=0\) gives convergence in expectation to zero, while \(b>0\) gives an asymptotic expected-error upper bound no larger than \(b/a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive one-step conditional bound yields geometric convergence of expected error, up to a residual floor caused by persistent additive noise.
assumptions_latex: \(E_k\geq0\) is integrable and adapted to \(\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}E_k\leq(1-a)^k\mathbb{E}E_0+(b/a)(1-(1-a)^k)\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative convergence error or merit value
asymptotic expected-error upper bound in the recursion

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Markov conversion of an expected nonnegative stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_K\geq0\) be a random convergence certificate, such as \(Z_K=\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\), and suppose \(\mathbb{E}Z_K\leq C/K\). Then for every confidence parameter \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z_K>\frac{C}{K\delta}\right)\leq\delta.\] Therefore \(K\geq C/(\delta\varepsilon^2)\) guarantees \(Z_K\leq\varepsilon^2\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\). This is the direct single-run guarantee; independent repetition with a verifiable certificate may improve the confidence dependence when an appropriate selection rule is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An O(1/K) expected nonnegative certificate yields a single-run high-probability guarantee with iteration cost proportional to 1/(delta epsilon squared) by Markov's inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\geq C/(\delta\varepsilon^2)\Rightarrow\mathbb{P}(Z_K\leq\varepsilon^2)\geq1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative random convergence certificate after K iterations
constant in the expected convergence bound

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Sure Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RobbinsSiegmund-type criterion for almost-sure convergence of a random merit sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E_k)\), \((U_k)\), \((a_k)\), and \((b_k)\) be nonnegative processes adapted to \((\mathcal F_k)\), with \[\mathbb{E}[E_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq(1+a_k)E_k-U_k+b_k\quad\text{almost surely}.\] If \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty b_k<\infty\) almost surely, then \(E_k\) converges almost surely to a finite random variable and \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty U_k<\infty\) almost surely. In particular, if \(U_k\geq c\|\nabla f(x_k)\|^2\) for a constant \(c>0\), then \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable-error supermartingale recursion yields almost-sure convergence of the merit sequence and summability, hence vanishing, of the stationarity measure.
assumptions_latex: \(E_k,U_k,a_k,b_k\geq0\) are adapted and the displayed conditional expectation exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k\) converges almost surely and \(\sum_kU_k<\infty\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear ambient-dimension penalty for fixed-rank isotropic subspace sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the projected-gradient method in dimension \(d\) with a uniformly distributed rank-\(s\) orthogonal projector, where \(1\leq s\leq d\). Its capture factor is \(\rho=s/d\). Thus any full-gradient stationarity bound obtained by isotropic transfer from \[\mathbb{E}\|P_R\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\frac{2L\Delta_0}{K}\] becomes \[\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\frac{2L\Delta_0d}{Ks}.\] For fixed \(s\), achieving expected squared full-gradient norm at most \(\varepsilon^2\) therefore requires \(K\geq2L\Delta_0d/(s\varepsilon^2)\), displaying linear dependence on the ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed sketch rank, isotropic full-stationarity complexity grows linearly with ambient dimension because only the fraction s/d of gradient energy is captured.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is a uniform rank-\(s\) orthogonal projector and the update uses step \(1/L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\geq2L\Delta_0d/(s\varepsilon^2)\) suffices for \(\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\varepsilon^2\).

notation.meaning: initial objective gap to a finite lower bound

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace-Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse sketch-rank dependence of isotropic full-stationarity iteration complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the smooth lower-bounded projected-gradient model with a uniform rank-\(s\) orthogonal projector in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the expected full-gradient certificate satisfies \[\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\frac{2L\Delta_0d}{Ks}.\] Hence, for fixed ambient dimension \(d\), the unrounded sufficient iteration bound is inversely proportional to \(s\); increasing the subspace dimension from \(s_1\) to \(s_2\) multiplies that unrounded bound by \(s_1/s_2\). An integer sufficient count is \[K(s)=\left\lceil\frac{2L\Delta_0d}{s\varepsilon^2}\right\rceil.\] This conclusion concerns iteration count; the work per iteration can increase with \(s\) and must be accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For uniform isotropic sketches, the unrounded iteration bound decreases inversely with subspace dimension, although larger subspaces may cost more per iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth and bounded below with initial gap \(\Delta_0\).
\(P_k\) is a uniform rank-\(s\) orthogonal projector in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(s)=\lceil2L\Delta_0d/(s\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) is a sufficient integer iteration count.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Ratio Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterationwork tradeoff governed by the sketch ratio for dense subspace updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta=s/d\in(0,1]\) be the sketch ratio for a uniform rank-\(s\) projector. The isotropic stationarity bound has iteration count \(K=O(\theta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-2})\). If forming and applying a dense subspace update costs \(W_{\mathrm{iter}}(s,d)=O(ds)\), then the corresponding arithmetic work is \[K W_{\mathrm{iter}}=O\!\left(\frac{d}{s\varepsilon^2}\,ds\right)=O(d^2\varepsilon^{-2}),\] excluding objective, gradient, and sketch-construction costs. Thus increasing \(s\) improves the iteration count linearly but need not improve total dense linear-algebra work; benefits require cheaper structured sketches, parallelism, or reduced overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger sketch ratio reduces iterations, but with dense O(ds) updates the leading iteration savings can cancel against higher per-iteration work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K W_{\mathrm{iter}}=O(d^2\varepsilon^{-2})\) under the stated dense-cost model.

notation.meaning: fraction of ambient dimensions sampled per iteration
iteration count required by the stationarity bound

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic-Dimension Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient dimension is replaced by an invariant active-subspace dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume there is a fixed subspace \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) of dimension \(r\) such that \(\nabla f(x_k)\in U\) for every iterate. Let \(P_k\) project onto a uniformly sampled \(s\)-dimensional subspace of \(U\), using \(q=\min\{s,r\}\). Then \(\mathbb{E}[P_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=(q/r)P_U\), so \[\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\frac{2L\Delta_0r}{Kq}.\] Consequently, \(K\geq2L\Delta_0r/(q\varepsilon^2)\) suffices for expected squared full-gradient norm at most \(\varepsilon^2\), independently of the ambient dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all gradients lie in an r-dimensional active subspace and sketches sample that subspace isotropically, complexity depends on r rather than ambient dimension d.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth and bounded below with initial gap \(\Delta_0\).
A fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace \(U\) contains every \(\nabla f(x_k)\).
The sampled projector is uniform of rank \(q=\min\{s,r\}\) within \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\geq2L\Delta_0r/(q\varepsilon^2)\Rightarrow\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\leq\varepsilon^2\).

notation.meaning: fixed active subspace containing all encountered gradients
intrinsic dimension of the active subspace
orthogonal projector onto the active subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the intrinsic-dimension specialization, and the statement inconsistently describes an s-dimensional subspace of U while assigning the actual rank q=min{s,r}; an s-dimensional subspace of U does not exist when s>r. An authoritative result is needed to determine the intended sampling model and hypotheses.

children.title: Effective-Rank Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior governed by spectral mass or effective rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Effective-Rank Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral effective rank as a dimension surrogate for anisotropic sketch analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero positive-semidefinite matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\), define its effective rank by \[r_{\mathrm{eff}}(H)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(H)}{\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i(H)}{\max_i\lambda_i(H)}.\] It satisfies \(1\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(H)\leq\operatorname{rank}(H)\leq d\). A subspace-method complexity claim is genuinely effective-rank dependent only if its dimension factor can be bounded using \(r_{\mathrm{eff}}(H)\) and accompanying spectral quantities, without replacing them by \(d\). Effective rank alone does not control the smallest sketch-capture eigenvalue, so an additional alignment or spectral-tail condition is required for full-space stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Effective rank measures spectral spread, but it can replace ambient dimension in complexity only with additional sketch-alignment or spectral-tail control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(H)\leq\operatorname{rank}(H)\leq d\), and effective rank alone does not ensure uniform gradient capture.

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite covariance, curvature, or data operator relevant to sketching

Its selected kind, condition, also does not match the terminal complexity container. children.title: Rank-Mismatch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Performance loss when selected sketch scales misrepresent effective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Mismatch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stationarity fails to imply ambient stationarity when sketches miss active directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a fixed subspace of dimension \(s<d\), with projector \(P_V\), and choose a nonzero vector \(u\in V^\perp\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x-u\|^2\) at \(x=0\), \[P_V\nabla f(0)=P_V(-u)=0,\qquad \|\nabla f(0)\|=\|u\|>0.\] Hence exact stationarity in every searched direction of \(V\) does not imply full-space stationarity. More generally, if the sketch distribution has mean projector \(M=\mathbb{E}P\) with \(\lambda_{\min}(M)=0\), no finite constant can bound \(\|g\|^2\) by \(\mathbb{E}\|Pg\|^2\) for all \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sketch rank or support misses an active direction, projected gradients may vanish while the full gradient remains nonzero; uniform stationarity transfer then fails.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a proper linear subspace and \(u\in V^\perp\setminus\{0\}\).

children.title: Sketch-Dimension Requirements
children.top_down_role: Reduced dimensions needed for targeted geometric or optimization quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Dimension Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient Gaussian sketch size for embedding a fixed subspace with prescribed distortion and failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns, and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have independent \(N(0,1/m)\) entries. For \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(0<\delta<1\), there is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that the dimension condition \[m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\bigl(r+\log(1/\delta)\bigr)\] is sufficient to ensure, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), that \[(1-\varepsilon)\lVert Uz\rVert_2^2\leq \lVert SUz\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\lVert Uz\rVert_2^2\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{R}^r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian sketch embeds a fixed r-dimensional subspace with distortion epsilon and failure probability delta when its row count scales as epsilon^{-2}(r+log(1/delta)).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}(r+\log(1/\delta))\) suffices for an \(\varepsilon\)-subspace embedding with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gaussian fixed-subspace embedding condition is mathematically standard, appropriately classified as a condition, and consistent across the LaTeX and plain statements. However, no source is supplied for the uniform embedding bound or its dependence on r, epsilon, and delta.

children.title: Confidence-Level Dependence
children.top_down_role: Resource dependence on the desired probability of successful preservation.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Level Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional sketch dimension needed to increase the success probability of a fixed-subspace embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the fixed-subspace Gaussian sketch model, suppose \(m_0\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}r\) rows provide the dimension-dependent part of the embedding requirement. Achieving failure probability at most \(\delta\in(0,1)\) is ensured by adding at most \(C\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta)\) rows, so that \[m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\bigl(r+\log(1/\delta)\bigr).\] Consequently, replacing \(\delta\) by \(\delta/q\), for \(q\ge1\), increases the sufficient row count by only \(C\varepsilon^{-2}\log q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher confidence costs only logarithmically many additional sketch rows: dividing the failure probability by q adds order epsilon^{-2} log q rows.
assumptions_latex: The sketched object is one fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace.
The sketch has independent normalized Gaussian entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(\delta/q)-m(\delta)\le C\varepsilon^{-2}\log q\) for the stated sufficient dimension rule.

notation.meaning: sufficient sketch dimension at failure level delta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic confidence dependence fits this complexity-bound leaf, but m(delta) is not defined as a particular sufficient rule or minimal dimension. Consequently, the asserted difference inequality does not follow merely from separate sufficient upper bounds, and an authoritative source is needed to fix the formulation and constants.

children.title: Dimension-Confidence Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Navigation across sketch size, reliability, and computational cost regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Confidence Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive interaction between intrinsic dimension and logarithmic confidence in Gaussian subspace embeddings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace and a normalized Gaussian sketch, a sufficient embedding dimension has the form \[m=C\varepsilon^{-2}\bigl(r+\log(1/\delta)\bigr).\] Thus intrinsic dimension and confidence contribute additively: the dimension term dominates when \(r\ge\log(1/\delta)\), whereas the confidence term dominates when \(r\le\log(1/\delta)\). At fixed distortion, doubling \(r\) changes the first term linearly, while exponentially reducing \(\delta\) changes the second term linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sketch size grows linearly with subspace dimension but only logarithmically with inverse failure probability; whichever term is larger controls the sufficient dimension.
assumptions_latex: The sketch is required to embed one fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace.
The sufficient Gaussian embedding bound applies for \(0<\varepsilon,\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m=O(\varepsilon^{-2}r+\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))\), with the crossover at \(r\asymp\log(1/\delta)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive dimension-confidence interpretation fits the property leaf, but the statement writes an exact equality m=C epsilon^{-2}(r+log(1/delta)) where only a sufficient lower threshold or asymptotic upper bound has been established. No source supports the underlying Gaussian embedding estimate or crossover interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden Full-Dimension Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource boundary separating reduced-coordinate arithmetic from operations that still touch the ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced optimization can retain full-dimensional gradient, projection, lifting, and storage costs, so an r-dimensional subproblem does not by itself yield n-independent complexity.
assumptions_latex: The iterate and full gradient are represented explicitly in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
The basis \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) is applied explicitly in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{iter}}\ge T_{\nabla}(n)+T_{P^{\mathsf T}}(n,r)+T_P(n,r)\), irrespective of \(T_{\mathrm{red}}(r)\).

notation.meaning: cost of producing the ambient gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and oracle accounting for obtaining a gradient restricted to an explicit subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an explicit basis \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), and a first-order oracle returning \(g=\nabla f(x)\), the projected-gradient oracle returns \(g_P=P^{\mathsf T}g\in\mathbb{R}^r\). Its cost is \[T_{\mathrm{PG}}(n,r)=T_{\nabla f}(x)+T_{P^{\mathsf T}}(n,r).\] For a dense materialized \(P\), the projection uses \(O(nr)\) arithmetic operations and reads \(O(nr)\) stored entries; structured or implicit bases replace this term by their actual application cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-gradient call costs one ambient gradient evaluation plus one basis-transpose application, which is O(nr) for a dense explicit basis.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns the full ambient gradient \(\nabla f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) has full column rank and is available explicitly or as an operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{PG}}=T_{\nabla f}+T_{P^{\mathsf T}}\), with \(T_{P^{\mathsf T}}=O(nr)\) for dense explicit \(P\).

children.title: Sketch-Formation Cost
children.top_down_role: Work and storage attributable to constructing a sketch representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Formation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of generating and storing an explicit sketch independently of applying it to problem data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sketching matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), define formation as generating its representation before any multiplication by data. A dense independent-entry sketch requires \(mn\) scalar draws or assignments, hence \(\Theta(mn)\) formation work and \(\Theta(mn)\) storage when materialized. A structured or seeded sketch has formation cost \(T_{\mathrm{gen}}(m,n)\) and representation size \(M_S(m,n)\), which must be reported separately from the cost of applying \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Materializing a dense m-by-n sketch costs Theta(mn) generation work and storage; implicit sketches instead use their generator and representation costs.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is formed before its first application.
Dense formation explicitly generates and stores every entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{form}}=\Theta(mn)\) and \(M_S=\Theta(mn)\) for dense materialization; implicit representations use \(T_{\mathrm{gen}}\) and \(M_S\).

children.title: Sketch-Application Cost

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Application Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-use arithmetic cost of applying an explicit or implicit sketch to vectors or matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(T_S(n,m)\) denote the work required to compute \(Sx\) for one \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(S\) is dense and materialized, \(T_S(n,m)=\Theta(mn)\). Applying the same sketch to \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times b}\) columnwise costs \(\Theta(mnb)\) by ordinary dense multiplication. For structured, sparse, or operator-defined sketches, resource accounting must use the corresponding application cost rather than the storage size or formation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense sketch-vector product costs Theta(mn), and sketching b columns costs Theta(mnb); structured sketches must be charged by their actual operator cost.
assumptions_latex: Ordinary dense matrix-vector or matrix-matrix multiplication is used for a materialized sketch.
\(X\) has \(b\) columns and no exploitable additional structure.

children.title: Materialization Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Materialization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision conditions distinguishing explicit, regenerated, and operator-only sketch representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sketch \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is in the explicit regime when all \(mn\) entries are stored; it is in the seeded regime when a seed and parameters are stored and entries are regenerated as needed; it is in the operator regime when only routines for \(x\mapsto Sx\) and, when required, \(y\mapsto S^{\mathsf T}y\) are available. Resource bounds must respectively charge explicit storage, regeneration work, or operator-application work, and must not silently identify these three costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sketches may be stored explicitly, regenerated from a seed, or exposed only as operators; each regime has distinct storage and application accounting.
assumptions_latex: The representation supports every sketch or adjoint application required by the algorithm.
Generation, storage, and application are counted as separate resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Subproblem Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle and arithmetic accounting for solving the optimization model restricted to a selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) and define the reduced model \(\phi(d)=f(x+Pd)\) on \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^r\). If a reduced solver performs \(q\) iterations, each using one value-gradient evaluation of \(\phi\) and \(A(r)\) additional arithmetic, its total cost is \[q\bigl(T_{\phi}(n,r)+A(r)\bigr),\qquad T_{\phi}(n,r)=T_f(x+Pd)+T_P(n,r)+T_{P^{\mathsf T}}(n,r).\] Any factorization, projection onto \(D\), or inner stopping test must be added separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving an r-dimensional model costs its reduced iterations times model-oracle and r-dimensional arithmetic costs, plus any setup, projection, factorization, and stopping-test costs.

Each reduced iteration evaluates both \(\phi(d)\) and \(\nabla\phi(d)=P^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x+Pd)\).

children.title: Memory Cost

Workspace shared across nonoverlapping operations is counted by its maximum concurrent size, not by summing all temporary allocations.

children.title: Data-Pass Cost

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Pass Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pass complexity for sketched methods operating on data too large to assume random-access residency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a dataset be partitioned into ordered blocks \(A_1,\ldots,A_B\). One data pass is one execution interval during which every block is read at least once and no block needs to be reread after the final block is processed. The pass cost of an algorithm is the number \(p\) of such complete traversals required to produce its output. Reading only a proper subset is charged fractionally or separately, and repeated access caused by insufficient memory begins an additional pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data-pass cost counts complete traversals of all dataset blocks; rereading blocks after a traversal or because of limited memory incurs another pass.
assumptions_latex: The data are organized into \(B\) externally readable blocks.
Block reads, rather than arithmetic operations, define the resource being measured.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pass complexity is \(p\), the number of complete ordered traversals needed before termination.

children.title: Communication Cost

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed resource accounting by synchronization rounds and transmitted scalar words.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a distributed implementation with \(p\) workers, define communication cost as the ordered pair \((R,W)\), where \(R\) is the number of synchronization rounds and \(W\) is the total number of scalar words transmitted across worker boundaries. If each of \(K\) iterations performs one all-reduce of an \(r\)-vector, then \(R=K\); under a tree implementation, the critical-path word traffic is \(O(Kr\log p)\), while aggregate network traffic is implementation-dependent and must be reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication should report both synchronization rounds and transmitted words; K tree all-reduces of r-vectors use K rounds and O(Kr log p) critical-path traffic.
assumptions_latex: There are \(p\ge2\) workers and \(K\) synchronous iterations.
Each iteration performs one tree-based all-reduce of an \(r\)-vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=K\) and \(W_{critical}=O(Kr\log p)\) under the stated tree communication model.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted stationarity certificate on the feasible sketched affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\). For \(x\in C\) and \(\eta>0\), set \(D_x=C\cap(x+\operatorname{range}Q)\) and define
\[
G_{Q,\eta}(x)=\eta^{-1}\bigl(x-P_{D_x}(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\bigr).
\]
The inequality \(\|G_{Q,\eta}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is a projected-gradient residual certificate for \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity on \(D_x\). Moreover, \(G_{Q,\eta}(x)=0\) if and only if \(\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in D_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected-gradient displacement measures stationarity over the feasible sketched affine subspace; it vanishes exactly when the corresponding restricted variational inequality holds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|G_{Q,\eta}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies restricted \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity, and \(G_{Q,\eta}(x)=0\) is equivalent to the restricted variational inequality.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the closed convex set D.
Matrix whose range is the trial subspace.
Projected-gradient residual mapping restricted to the sketched affine subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Model Decrease Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decrease certificate from a smooth upper model restricted to a trial subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\). Define the reduced upper model
\[
m_x(u)=\langle Q^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x),u\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\|Qu\|^2.
\]
For any computed reduced step \(u\), the smoothness inequality gives \(f(x+Qu)-f(x)\leq m_x(u)\). Consequently, a verifiable bound \(m_x(u)\leq-\Delta\), where \(\Delta>0\), certifies the full-objective decrease \(f(x+Qu)\leq f(x)-\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently negative smooth reduced model certifies at least the same decrease in the full objective along the lifted subspace step.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(z)\|\leq L\|y-z\|\) on every segment used by the step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x(u)\leq-\Delta\) implies \(f(x+Qu)\leq f(x)-\Delta\).

notation.meaning: Reduced smooth upper model for objective change.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Optimality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frank–Wolfe-type first-order gap over the current feasible subspace slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(x\in C\). For \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\), define \(D_x=C\cap(x+\operatorname{range}Q)\) and
\[
g_Q(x)=\max_{y\in D_x}\langle\nabla f(x),x-y\rangle.
\]
Then \(g_Q(x)\geq0\), and \(g_Q(x)=0\) exactly when \(\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for all \(y\in D_x\). Thus \(g_Q(x)\leq\varepsilon\) is a computable restricted optimality-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted gap maximizes linearized improvement over the feasible subspace slice and vanishes exactly at restricted first-order stationary points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_Q(x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies a restricted first-order gap of at most \(\varepsilon\), while \(g_Q(x)=0\) is equivalent to restricted stationarity.

notation.meaning: Feasible slice through x parallel to the trial subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and mathematics are precise: compactness ensures attainment, x belongs to the slice, and the zero-gap equivalence is correct. No source or inspectable locator is supplied for the restricted conditional-gradient gap, so the record cannot pass evidence review.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Capture Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transfer from a captured reduced gradient to the full gradient norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) have orthonormal columns and let \(g=\nabla f(x)\). A number \(\rho\in(0,1]\) is a gradient-capture certificate at \(x\) when
\[
\|Q^{\mathsf T}g\|\geq\rho\|g\|.
\]
If the reduced gradient also satisfies \(\|Q^{\mathsf T}g\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{red}}\), the two checked inequalities imply \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{red}}/\rho\). Thus reduced stationarity transfers to full-space stationarity only when a strictly positive capture factor has independently been certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound on the fraction of gradient norm seen by the subspace converts a reduced-gradient tolerance into a full-gradient tolerance.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the sampled trial subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, and the norm implication is mathematically correct. However, no source supports this gradient-capture certificate or its use as a reduced-to-full stationarity transfer condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding-Validity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral certificate for a sketch embedding on a specified relevant subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning a specified relevant subspace and let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\) be a sketch. For \(\delta\in[0,1)\), the computable condition
\[
\|U^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SU-I_r\|_2\leq\delta
\]
is an embedding-validity certificate. It is equivalent to
\[
(1-\delta)\|v\|^2\leq\|Sv\|^2\leq(1+\delta)\|v\|^2
\]
for every \(v\in\operatorname{range}U\), and therefore certifies norm preservation on that subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral-norm test on a basis Gram matrix certifies that the sketch preserves every norm in the designated relevant subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|U^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SU-I_r\|_2\leq\delta\) certifies a \((1\pm\delta)\) squared-norm embedding on \(\operatorname{range}U\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the relevant subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral certificate is correctly equivalent to the stated squared-norm bounds on range(U), and the content kind fits the terminal container. No source or locator is supplied for the subspace-embedding characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Residual Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct full-space check guarding against false convergence in a sampled subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. For \(x\in C\) and \(\eta>0\), compute
\[
R_\eta(x)=\eta^{-1}\bigl(x-P_C(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\bigr).
\]
A stopping decision is accepted only if \(\|R_\eta(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\), irrespective of any smaller restricted residual. The equality \(R_\eta(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for all \(y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before stopping, compute the projected-gradient residual over the entire feasible set; this prevents an uninformative subspace from falsely indicating stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|R_\eta(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) directly certifies full-space projected-gradient stationarity to tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the full feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Optimization: Algorithms and Consistent Approximations

source_witnesses.source_title: Optimization: Algorithms and Consistent Approximations

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Stopping Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided randomized certificate for a full-space residual at a stopping time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{F}\) denote the information available before drawing an independent validation sketch, let \(r(x)\geq0\) be the desired full-space residual, and let \(Z(x)\geq0\) be the validation statistic. Suppose a known \(c>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\) satisfy
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl(r(x)\leq cZ(x)\mid\mathcal{F}\bigr)\geq1-\delta.
\]
Then the rule that stops when \(Z(x)\leq\varepsilon/c\) certifies \(r(x)\leq\varepsilon\) with conditional probability at least \(1-\delta\). Repeated tests require a valid allocation of their failure probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent validation statistic with a one-sided confidence bound yields a high-probability stopping certificate; repeated validation must account for accumulated failure probability.
assumptions_latex: The validation randomness is fresh conditional on \(\mathcal{F}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On the event \(Z(x)\leq\varepsilon/c\), the assertion \(r(x)\leq\varepsilon\) has conditional confidence at least \(1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assumed bound directly gives a high-probability implication from acceptance to r(x)≤ε, but it does not by itself establish P(r(x)≤ε | F, Z(x)≤ε/c)≥1−δ. Thus the phrase 'conditional confidence' after observing acceptance is potentially overstated. A source and a precise simultaneous-event or selective-inference formulation are required, especially for repeated tests.

children.title: Specialized-Oracle Complexity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Boundary links to generic complexity families owned by neighboring chapters.

children.title: Finite-Sum Gradient Complexity Interface
children.top_down_role: Component and subspace sampling interactions only.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Gradient Complexity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting interface for component sampling combined with reduced directional-gradient queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}f_i(x)\). At iteration \(k\), choose a component batch \(B_k\) of size \(b_k\) and a subspace basis \(Q_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q_k}\). If the oracle returns \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}\nabla f_i(x_k)\) for each \(i\in B_k\), then through iteration \(K-1\) the component-gradient count is
\[
C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}b_k,
\]
and the returned scalar directional-derivative count is
\[
D_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}b_kq_k.
\]
A full batch contributes \(N\) component queries, independently of \(q_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface separately counts sampled component gradients and their reduced directional coordinates, exposing how batch sizes and subspace dimensions interact.
assumptions_latex: Iteration \(k\) queries every \(i\in B_k\) once in \(q_k\) directions.
Oracle overhead beyond returned directional derivatives is excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resource totals are \(C_K=\sum_{k<K}b_k\) component queries and \(D_K=\sum_{k<K}b_kq_k\) scalar directional derivatives.

notation.meaning: Number of sampled finite-sum components at iteration k.
Dimension of the sampled trial subspace.
Cumulative component and scalar directional-query counts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is suitable for the oracle-interface leaf, and the two totals are internally consistent under the explicitly stated oracle model. No source supports treating one returned reduced component gradient as one component query and b_k q_k scalar directional derivatives, so the accounting convention needs evidence.

children.title: Proximal-Oracle Complexity Interface
children.top_down_role: Subspace-proximal accounting only.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Oracle Complexity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting for exact or iterative proximal solves in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a composite objective \(F=f+h\), a subspace-proximal oracle at \((x,Q,z,\eta)\) returns
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}^q}\left\{h(x+Qu)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\|u-z\|^2\right\},
\]
when the minimizer exists. If outer iteration \(k\) invokes this oracle \(t_k\) times in dimension \(q_k\), then after \(K\) iterations its exact call complexity is \(P_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}t_k\), with dimensional workload recorded as \(W_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}t_kq_k\). For one call per iteration, \(P_K=K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subspace-proximal complexity counts reduced proximal solves separately from their dimensions; one exact solve per outer iteration gives exactly one oracle call per iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each recorded invocation returns an exact reduced minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal-oracle count is \(P_K=\sum_{k<K}t_k\), and the dimension-weighted accounting quantity is \(W_K=\sum_{k<K}t_kq_k\).

notation.meaning: Number of reduced proximal-oracle calls at outer iteration k.
Dimension of the reduced proximal problem.

source_refs.source_title: First-Order Methods in Optimization

source_witnesses.source_title: First-Order Methods in Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic proximal-gradient citation does not clearly support the specialized reduced oracle or the dimension-weighted quantity W_K. The call-count identity is valid by definition, but the mathematical oracle model and workload interpretation require a source specific enough to justify this interface.

children.title: Conditional-Gradient Oracle Complexity Interface
children.top_down_role: Restricted and sketched linear-oracle accounting only.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Gradient Oracle Complexity Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Call accounting for linear minimization over restricted feasible subspace slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and convex. At iteration \(k\), define \(D_k=C\cap(x_k+\operatorname{range}Q_k)\). A restricted linear-minimization oracle returns
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D_k}\langle g_k,y\rangle.
\]
If iteration \(k\) makes \(\ell_k\) such calls, then the cumulative restricted-oracle complexity through iteration \(K-1\) is \(L_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\ell_k\). Hence a method making one restricted call per iteration uses exactly \(K\) calls; any full-set calls over \(C\) must be counted separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional-gradient accounting totals linear-oracle calls over feasible subspace slices and keeps any full-feasible-set calls in a separate resource category.
assumptions_latex: A call returns an exact minimizer of the displayed linear problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted linear-oracle count is \(L_K=\sum_{k<K}\ell_k\), equal to \(K\) when \(\ell_k=1\) for every iteration.

notation.meaning: Feasible slice induced by the current subspace.
Restricted linear-oracle calls at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal interface, and compactness plus nonempty slices ensures exact restricted linear minimizers exist. The cumulative count is correct under the declared model, but no conditional-gradient or restricted-oracle source is supplied.

children.title: Adaptive Optimization Implementation Interface
children.top_down_role: Policies controlling subspace fidelity and computational resources without procedural detail.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Sketch-Size Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subspace-gradient scheme with constant subspace dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(x_0\in C\), fixed \(q\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), sample \(Q_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) with orthonormal columns, set \(D_k=C\cap(x_k+\operatorname{range}Q_k)\), and update
\[
x_{k+1}=P_{D_k}\bigl(x_k-\eta_k\nabla f(x_k)\bigr).
\]
The sketch-size policy keeps \(\dim(\operatorname{range}Q_k)=q\) for every \(k\). Stop and output \(x_k\) only when a prescribed full-space residual test is at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise continue with a fresh sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every iteration uses a fresh subspace of the same dimension, while termination is governed by a specified full-space residual rather than the sampled subspace alone.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy produces feasible iterates with constant sketch size \(q\) and returns the first iterate passing the prescribed full-space tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate role for this concrete fixed-size policy, and the projection keeps every iterate feasible. No source supports the combined fresh-sketch update, constant-dimension policy, and mandatory full-space stopping check; the sampling and step-size framework also remains method-dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Progressive Sketch-Size Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subspace-gradient scheme with a scheduled nondecreasing sketch dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(x_0\in C\), \(q_0\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), growth factor \(\gamma>1\), stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), sample an orthonormal \(Q_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q_k}\), define \(D_k=C\cap(x_k+\operatorname{range}Q_k)\), and set
\[
x_{k+1}=P_{D_k}\bigl(x_k-\eta_k\nabla f(x_k)\bigr),\qquad q_{k+1}=\min\{n,\lceil\gamma q_k\rceil\}.
\]
Stop and output \(x_k\) when the prescribed full-space residual is at most \(\varepsilon\). Thus \(q_k\) is nondecreasing and reaches \(n\) after finitely many scheduled increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subspace dimension grows geometrically up to the ambient dimension, while a full-space residual supplies the stopping decision.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule satisfies \(q_{k+1}\geq q_k\), \(q_k\leq n\), and \(q_k=n\) after finitely many increases unless termination occurs earlier.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits this concrete progressive policy, and the geometric capped schedule is nondecreasing and reaches n after finitely many updates. No source supports this particular growth schedule together with the projected subspace-gradient update and full-space stopping rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Driven Fidelity Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive sketch dimension selected by a computable fidelity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(S_{k,1},\ldots,S_{k,J}\) be candidate sketches of nondecreasing fidelity. For each \(j\), form a sketched direction \(d_{k,j}\) and a computable certificate \(c_{k,j}\ge 0\) bounding its prescribed model or gradient discrepancy. Given tolerance \(\tau_k>0\), select \(j_k=\min\{j:c_{k,j}\le\tau_k\}\), if this set is nonempty, and output \(d_k=d_{k,j_k}\). If no candidate passes, output a full-fidelity direction or declare fidelity failure. The policy must record \(c_{k,j_k}\), \(\tau_k\), and the selected fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate increasingly faithful sketches until a computable discrepancy certificate meets tolerance; otherwise use full fidelity or report failure.
assumptions_latex: \(c_{k,j}\) is computable and valid for the discrepancy specified by the implementation.
Candidate fidelities are ordered from least to most expensive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_{k,j_k}\le\tau_k\) whenever a certified candidate is returned.

notation.meaning: candidate sketch at iteration k and fidelity level j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the policy leaf, but the certificate is defined only as a model- or gradient-discrepancy bound. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required to determine the discrepancy, validity conditions, and justified fallback behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Distribution Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-independent sampling law for coordinate or block sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix nonempty blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and probabilities \(p_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^q p_i=1\). At every iteration \(k\), independently of the current iterate and past samples, draw \(I_k\) from the fixed law \(\mathbb{P}(I_k=i)=p_i\). Construct the sketch \(S_k\) from the coordinate columns indexed by \(B_{I_k}\), evaluate the corresponding restricted first-order information, and return the resulting sketched direction. The probability vector and block family remain unchanged throughout the run; only the realized index varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iteration, sample a coordinate block from one unchanged probability distribution and construct the sketch from that block.
assumptions_latex: The random indices \((I_k)_{k\ge0}\) are independent of the iterate history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(I_k=i\mid I_0,\ldots,I_{k-1},x_0,\ldots,x_k)=p_i\) for every \(i\) and \(k\).

notation.meaning: fixed probability assigned to block i

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Importance-Driven Sampling
children.top_down_role: Sampling policies prioritized by component or coordinate importance information.

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Driven Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling probabilities determined by positive importance scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), assign each candidate block \(B_i\) a finite importance score \(a_{k,i}\ge0\). Choose a floor parameter \(\varepsilon>0\) and define \(p_{k,i}=(a_{k,i}+\varepsilon)/(\sum_{j=1}^q a_{k,j}+q\varepsilon)\). Draw \(I_k\) conditionally on the available history according to \(\mathbb{P}(I_k=i\mid\mathcal{F}_k)=p_{k,i}\), form the sketch from \(B_{I_k}\), and output the associated sketched first-order direction. If an unbiased full-vector estimator is required, scale the sampled block contribution by \(1/p_{k,I_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert nonnegative importance scores into positive sampling probabilities, sample a block, and optionally apply inverse-probability correction.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{k,i}\ge0\) is finite and measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{F}_k\).
Every sampled block contribution is available when selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{k,i}>0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^q p_{k,i}=1\), and inverse-probability weighting is conditionally unbiased for the sum of block contributions.

notation.meaning: information available before sampling at iteration k

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability formula is mathematically coherent and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the cited chapter-level coordinate-update locator does not specifically support this score-to-probability rule or the optional inverse-probability estimator. A direct authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Residual-Driven Sampling
children.top_down_role: Sampling policies prioritized by current residual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Driven Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive block sampling driven by current residual magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k=(r_{k,1},\ldots,r_{k,q})\) be block residuals measurable before sampling. For an exponent \(\gamma>0\) and floor \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(w_{k,i}=\lVert r_{k,i}\rVert^\gamma+\varepsilon\) and \(p_{k,i}=w_{k,i}/\sum_{j=1}^q w_{k,j}\). Draw \(I_k\) conditionally according to \(p_{k,i}\), construct a sketch containing block \(I_k\), and update the residual information after the trial step. Thus blocks with larger current residual norm receive larger sampling probability, while the positive floor preserves exploration of every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample blocks in proportion to powered residual magnitude plus a positive exploration floor.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_{k,i}\) is finite and measurable before the iteration-k draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lVert r_{k,i}\rVert>\lVert r_{k,j}\rVert\), then \(p_{k,i}>p_{k,j}\), while \(p_{k,i}>0\) for every block.

notation.meaning: current residual associated with block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed residual-priority rule is internally coherent, but no source establishes this particular powered-residual policy or the meaning and validity of the block residuals in the sketched first-order setting.

children.title: Hybrid Priority Sampling
children.top_down_role: Policies that combine importance signals with residual signals when selecting samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Priority Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex mixture of importance, residual, and exploration priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(q\ge 1\) and let \(u_{k,i}\ge0\) and \(v_{k,i}\ge0\) be importance and residual scores for blocks \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Normalize them as \(\widehat u_{k,i}=(u_{k,i}+\varepsilon)/(\sum_{j=1}^q u_{k,j}+q\varepsilon)\) and \(\widehat v_{k,i}=(v_{k,i}+\varepsilon)/(\sum_{j=1}^q v_{k,j}+q\varepsilon)\), where \(\varepsilon>0\). Given \(\lambda_k,\delta_k\ge0\) with \(\lambda_k+\delta_k\le1\), set \(p_{k,i}=\lambda_k\widehat u_{k,i}+\delta_k\widehat v_{k,i}+(1-\lambda_k-\delta_k)/q\). Sample a block from \(p_k\) and construct the corresponding sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite family of blocks, mix normalized importance, residual, and uniform-exploration distributions, then sample the sketch block from the resulting distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{k,i}>0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^q p_{k,i}=1\).

children.title: Partial Sketch Refresh
children.top_down_role: Policies that replace only selected portions of a current sketch.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Sketch Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refreshes selected sketch columns while retaining the remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the iteration-k sketch by an ordered sample tuple \(I_k=(i_{k,1},\ldots,i_{k,m})\). Choose a refresh set \(R_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For positions \(\ell\notin R_k\), set \(i_{k+1,\ell}=i_{k,\ell}\); for \(\ell\in R_k\), draw \(i_{k+1,\ell}\) from a specified conditional distribution \(P_{k,\ell}\). Construct \(S_{k+1}\) from the resulting tuple. Full refresh corresponds to \(R_k=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), while \(R_k=\varnothing\) leaves the sketch unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain designated sketch entries and resample only positions selected by the refresh rule.
assumptions_latex: The sketch has \(m\ge1\) identifiable sample positions.
Each \(P_{k,\ell}\) is a probability distribution on the admissible sample set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i_{k+1,\ell}=i_{k,\ell}\) for every \(\ell\notin R_k\), and exactly \(\lvert R_k\rvert\) positions are eligible for replacement.

notation.meaning: ordered tuple defining the current sketch
set of positions selected for refresh

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and retain-versus-resample construction fit the leaf, but no source supports the tuple model, conditional replacement laws, or the assumptions governing dependence and duplicate samples.

children.title: Sample Recycling
children.top_down_role: Policies governing reuse of previously acquired samples or sketch components.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample Recycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuses previously evaluated samples subject to an explicit validity test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pool \(\mathcal{P}_k\) of stored samples, each containing an index, its evaluated first-order datum, and the point and iteration at which it was computed. Given a validity predicate \(V_k(z)\in\{0,1\}\), form the recyclable set \(\mathcal{R}_k=\{z\in\mathcal{P}_k:V_k(z)=1\}\). Build the iteration-k sketch from selected elements of \(\mathcal{R}_k\) and newly drawn samples, evaluating only the new samples. After the iteration, insert new records and discard records failing the next validity test. A recycled datum may be used only with any correction required by the declared estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse stored sample evaluations that pass a declared validity test, draw replacements as needed, and record any estimator correction.
assumptions_latex: Every stored record identifies its sampling index and evaluation point.
\(V_k\) is computable before a stored sample is reused.
Required bias or staleness corrections are specified by the estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only records in \(\mathcal{R}_k\) contribute as recycled data at iteration \(k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record is an appropriate algorithmic interface for sample recycling, but its mathematical reliability depends on the unspecified validity predicate and estimator correction. A source must state conditions under which stale evaluations can be reused without invalidating the estimator.

children.title: Coupled Refresh-Recycling Policies
children.top_down_role: Coordination of selective replacement with retained sketch information.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Refresh-Recycling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jointly selects retained, recycled, and newly sampled sketch components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), partition the \(m\) sketch positions into disjoint sets \(K_k\), \(C_k\), and \(N_k\), denoting unchanged positions, positions filled from a valid recycling pool, and positions filled by new draws. Require \(K_k\cup C_k\cup N_k=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Copy entries in \(K_k\), assign distinct or replacement-eligible valid records to \(C_k\) according to the declared recycling rule, and sample entries in \(N_k\) from the current sampling law. The coupled policy chooses this partition from a refresh diagnostic, recycling validity, and the sampling budget, then records all three position sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly partition sketch positions into unchanged, recycled, and newly sampled components using diagnostics, validity, and budget.
assumptions_latex: The current sketch has \(m\ge1\) identifiable positions.
Recycled records pass the active validity predicate.
The new-sample law is defined whenever \(N_k\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every output position is supplied exactly once by retention, recycling, or a new draw.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-way partition is internally consistent and appropriate for an algorithm leaf, but the diagnostic, recycling rule, and sampling-budget coupling are an unsupported policy template rather than a sourced method.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation-Triggered Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh event triggered by insufficient progress over a finite window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_k\ge0\) be a monitored merit or residual value, choose a window \(w\ge1\), threshold \(\theta\in[0,1)\), and cooldown \(c\ge0\). For \(k\ge w\), declare stagnation when no refresh occurred during the preceding \(c\) iterations and \(\phi_k\ge(1-\theta)\phi_{k-w}\). Upon stagnation, replace the prescribed portion of the current sketch using the active sampling law and record a refresh event; otherwise retain the ordinary refresh schedule. If \(\phi_{k-w}=0\), stagnation is declared only when \(\phi_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the sketch when monitored progress over a fixed window falls below a threshold, subject to a cooldown rule.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_k\ge0\) is evaluated consistently across the monitoring window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A refresh is triggered whenever the stated stagnation predicate and cooldown condition both hold.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the refresh-policy leaf, but the exact windowed inequality, cooldown interpretation, and zero-baseline exception are design choices without cited support. A direct authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Stepsize Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces through which subspace methods receive or expose stepsize choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract for selecting an admissible step along a sketched direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a direction \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and an objective oracle for \(f\), a stepsize interface returns \(\alpha_k\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\) or a failure flag. For Armijo calibration, with \(0<\sigma<1\) and \(\nabla f(x_k)^\top d_k<0\), it must return a tested value satisfying \(f(x_k+\alpha_k d_k)\le f(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^\top d_k\). The interface records the trial values and evaluations and outputs \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) only after acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a bounded accepted stepsize satisfying the declared line-search condition, or report calibration failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful return satisfies the declared bounds and Armijo inequality before \(x_{k+1}\) is formed.
