knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Sketch Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary for reduced coordinates formed with a nonorthogonal sketch basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have full column rank, let \(G=B^{\mathsf T}B\), and let \(d=-BG^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}g\). If the computed Gram matrix is \(\widehat G=G+E\) and \(\lVert G^{-1}E\rVert_2<1\), then \(\widehat G\) is invertible and \(\lVert\widehat G^{-1}\rVert_2\le \lVert G^{-1}\rVert_2/(1-\lVert G^{-1}E\rVert_2)\). Moreover, \(\kappa_2(G)=\kappa_2(B)^2\). Under a relative perturbation model \(\lVert E\rVert_2\le c u\lVert G\rVert_2\), the sufficient stability condition becomes \(c u\kappa_2(B)^2<1\); when this quantity is not small, no uniform small relative-error bound follows from this perturbation estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forming a Gram system from a nonorthogonal sketch squares the basis condition number. Under a standard relative perturbation model, the inverse bound deteriorates when unit roundoff times that squared condition number is not small.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation satisfies \(\lVert E\rVert_2\le c u\lVert G\rVert_2\) for some \(c\ge0\) and \(u\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[c u\kappa_2(B)^2\not\ll 1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the inverse-perturbation estimate gives no uniform small-error guarantee}.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete distortion caused by treating a nonorthogonal computed basis as orthonormal.

The true orthogonal projector onto \(operatorname{range}(Q)\) is \(qq^top\). Thus loss of orthogonality doubles the projected step and changes the reduced norm by \(sqrt2\), even though the represented subspace is only one-dimensional.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Instability

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-sensitivity boundary for a sketch-derived positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(\widehat M=M+E\). If \(\lVert M^{-1}E\rVert_2<1\), then \(\widehat M\) is invertible and \(\lVert\widehat M^{-1}-M^{-1}\rVert_2\le \lVert M^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert E\rVert_2/(1-\lVert M^{-1}E\rVert_2)\). Since \(\lVert M^{-1}E\rVert_2\le \lVert E\rVert_2/\lambda_{\min}(M)\), the norm-based stability guarantee degenerates as \(\lVert E\rVert_2\) approaches \(\lambda_{\min}(M)\). At or beyond that scale, suitable symmetric perturbations can make \(\widehat M\) singular or indefinite, so no uniform inverse-stability guarantee remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The norm-based inverse-stability guarantee deteriorates when preconditioner error approaches the smallest eigenvalue. At that scale, some perturbations can make the computed preconditioner singular or indefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is a symmetric construction or rounding perturbation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lVert E\rVert_2\to\lambda_{\min}(M)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{degeneration of the stated uniform inverse-stability bound}.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Stage Error Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of sketch and preconditioner errors through their composed direction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact pipeline output be \(d=PSg\), and let the computed output be \(\widehat d=(P+Delta P)((S+Delta S)g+e)\). Then \(\widehat d-d=PDelta Sg+Pe+Delta PSg+Delta PDelta Sg+Delta Pe\), so \(\lVert\widehat d-d\rVert_2\) is bounded by the sum of the corresponding products of operator and error norms. In particular, upstream sketch error is multiplied by \(\lVert P\rVert_2\), while preconditioner error acts on the possibly large sketched vector. Separate small stagewise errors therefore do not imply a small final error when either stage has large gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors from sketching and preconditioning multiply across stages; small local errors can yield a large final direction when either stage has high gain.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Certificate Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance floor for certificates computed from a rounded sketched residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact reduced residual be \(r=S^top g\), and suppose finite-precision evaluation returns \(\widehat r=r+e\) with \(\lVert e\rVert_2\leeta\lVert S\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2\). Acceptance of \(\lVert\widehat r\rVert_2\levarepsilon\) implies only \(\lVert S^top g\rVert_2\levarepsilon+eta\lVert S\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2\). Therefore the computed test cannot certify the exact reduced tolerance \(varepsilon\) unless the rounding term is independently controlled. Moreover, without a lower embedding bound on the admissible gradients, a small reduced residual does not certify a small full-space norm \(\lVert g\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rounded reduced residual certifies only an enlarged tolerance, and it says nothing about the full gradient without an embedding lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The stated forward-error bound holds with \(eta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lVert\widehat r\rVert_2\levarepsilonquad\Longrightarrow\quad\lVert S^top g\rVert_2\levarepsilon+eta\lVert S\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2.\]
review_flags: finite-precision model and embedding qualification require a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The enlarged-tolerance implication follows from the triangle inequality, and the qualification about a missing lower embedding bound is correct. A dedicated finite-precision or sketch-embedding source is nevertheless required, and the LaTeX contains multiple missing command backslashes.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlated Worker Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perfectly correlated workers provide no aggregate subspace-coverage gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge2\) workers use rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors \(P_1,\ldots,P_p\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Suppose \(P_1=\cdots=P_p=P\) almost surely. Then the aggregate explored space \(\sum_{i=1}^p\operatorname{range}(P_i)\) equals \(\operatorname{range}(P)\) and has dimension \(r\), rather than potentially reaching \(pr\). If \(P\) is Haar-uniform and \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is fixed, then \(\mathbb{E}\lVert Pg\rVert_2^2=(r/n)\lVert g\rVert_2^2\), independently of \(p\). Thus perfectly correlated workers provide no aggregate subspace-coverage gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all workers use the same random rank-r subspace, their aggregate explored space still has dimension r and captures the same expected gradient energy as one worker.
assumptions_latex: The common projector \(P\) is Haar-uniform among rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\dim\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^p\operatorname{range}(P_i)\right)=r,\qquad \mathbb{E}\lVert Pg\rVert_2^2=\frac{r}{n}\lVert g\rVert_2^2.\]

notation.meaning: common projector used by all perfectly correlated workers

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Asynchronous Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step delay shrinks the stepsize interval guaranteeing convergence for all initial states, even in one dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and the one-step-stale update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha x_{k-1}\). Its characteristic polynomial is \(\lambda^2-\lambda+\alpha\). Both roots lie strictly inside the unit disk exactly when \(0<\alpha<1\), so this is the stepsize interval guaranteeing convergence for every initial pair \((x_{-1},x_0)\). By contrast, the synchronous update \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_k\) converges for every \(x_0\) when \(0<\alpha<2\). Hence for each \(\alpha\in[1,2)\), synchronous convergence is guaranteed while the stale recurrence has nonzero initial data for which it does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the scalar quadratic, one-step delay reduces the stepsize interval guaranteeing convergence for all initial states from zero-to-two to zero-to-one.
assumptions_latex: The asynchronous delay is exactly one iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\alpha\in[1,2)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{synchronous convergence for all initial values, but no such guarantee for the stale update}.\]

notation.meaning: characteristic root of the delayed recurrence

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Dominated Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock non-improvement boundary for synchronized parallel subspace iterations under an additive communication model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(p\) workers execute \(N_p(\varepsilon)\) synchronized iterations. Let \(C_p\ge0\) be per-iteration local computation time, \(L_p\ge0\) communication latency, \(B_p\ge0\) communicated bytes, and \(\beta_p>0\) effective bandwidth. Under a nonoverlapping additive cost model, \(T_p(\varepsilon)=N_p(\varepsilon)(C_p+L_p+B_p/\beta_p)\). Let a serial full-space method take \(T_1(\varepsilon)=N_1(\varepsilon)C_1\). If \(N_p(\varepsilon)(L_p+B_p/\beta_p)\ge T_1(\varepsilon)-N_p(\varepsilon)C_p\), then \(T_p(\varepsilon)\ge T_1(\varepsilon)\). Thus communication consumes all computational savings in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the stated synchronized additive cost model, parallel sketching cannot reduce wall time when latency and data-transfer time are at least the computational savings relative to serial execution.
assumptions_latex: Communication and local computation do not overlap.
Every synchronized iteration incurs the stated communication cost.
The serial and parallel methods use the same accuracy criterion \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_p(\varepsilon)\left(L_p+\frac{B_p}{\beta_p}\right)\ge T_1(\varepsilon)-N_p(\varepsilon)C_p\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T_p(\varepsilon)\ge T_1(\varepsilon).\]

notation.meaning: parallel wall time to accuracy epsilon

knowledge_statements.title: Feedback-Induced Sampling Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive sketch selection can invalidate conditional unbiasedness and isotropic coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), and let the nonzero vector \(g_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be measurable with respect to the history \(\mathcal{F}_k\). Define \(j\) as the smallest index with \(g_{k,j}\ne0\), choose any index \(\ell\ne j\), and set \(s_k=(g_{k,j}e_\ell-g_{k,\ell}e_j)/\sqrt{g_{k,j}^2+g_{k,\ell}^2}\). Then \(s_k\) is an \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable unit vector satisfying \(s_k^{\mathsf T}g_k=0\), so \(\mathbb{E}[\lvert s_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\rvert^2\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=0\). An independent uniformly distributed unit vector instead satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[\lvert s_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\rvert^2\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=\lVert g_k\rVert_2^2/n\). Thus history-dependent selection can destroy the conditional isotropic-coverage identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable feedback policy can select a unit direction orthogonal to the current nonzero gradient, making conditional captured energy zero instead of the positive value obtained under independent isotropic sampling.
assumptions_latex: The adaptive policy may use all information in \(\mathcal{F}_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb{E}[\lvert s_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\rvert^2\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=0\ne\frac{1}{n}\lVert g_k\rVert_2^2.\]

notation.meaning: history available before selecting the current sketch
